closest.title: Making Every Verified Token Count: Adaptive Verification for MoE Speculative Decoding
closest.evidence: EVICT ... truncating the draft tree before target verification and retaining only the cost-effective prefix ... combines them with offline-profiled verification cost
closest.why: Uses speculate-and-verify style cost/benefit gating around MoE expert activation to cut verification cost, but at the sequence/tree level for draft-model speculative decoding, not top-1 vs top-2 router disagreement checking within a single forward pass.

closest.title: AcceptMoE: Commitment-Weighted Self-Sizing Verifier Expert Sets for Efficient MoE Speculative Decoding
closest.evidence: a verifier-side expert selector that combines target-router scores with offline-estimated commitment probabilities and automatically adjusts the number of eligible experts for each verification block
closest.why: Also conditions expert computation on a confidence/commitment signal to reduce cost in MoE speculative decoding, but operates in the draft-target speculative decoding setting (accepting draft tokens) rather than proxying top-2 mixture disagreement for a single top-1 forward pass.

closest.title: Spend Experts Where You Are Unsure: Confidence-Adaptive Routing for Mixture-of-Experts LoRA
closest.evidence: Experts are activated in decreasing router weight until their cumulative mass reaches a threshold, with a small extension when the admitted experts disagree.
closest.why: This is the closest mechanism match: it uses router confidence/disagreement to decide whether to activate additional experts beyond top-1, directly analogous to the proposal's disagreement-triggered top-2 computation, though applied to MoE-LoRA adapters rather than exactly matching top-2 mixture via a distilled proxy and speculate-verify framing.

survives: The proposal's specific twist—using a cheap distilled/low-rank proxy to predict top-2 disagreement before deciding to compute the real second expert, framed explicitly as speculate-and-verify with exact top-2 recovery guarantee on the disagreement subset—is not clearly present in CARE (which uses the router's own softmax mass/disagreement directly rather than a separate trained proxy network) or the speculative-decoding papers (which operate on draft-token trees, not single-token top-1-vs-top-2 disagreement), so a version centered on the proxy-network verification-with-exact-fallback guarantee could still be new.

closest.title: DAG-MoE: From Simple Mixture to Structural Aggregation in Mixture-of-Experts
closest.evidence: replacing the standard weighted-summation aggregation with structural aggregation expands the expert-combination space without altering the experts or router, and enables possible multi-step reasoning within a single MoE layer
closest.why: targets non-additive, structured combination of already-selected experts via a learned module, close in spirit but operates on aggregation not on iterative energy-based selection of the expert subset itself.

closest.title: SDG-MoE: Signed Debate Graph Mixture-of-Experts
closest.evidence: adds a lightweight, iterative deliberation step before final aggregation ... a signed message-passing step that updates expert representations before aggregation
closest.why: introduces iterative refinement among selected experts to capture reinforcing/corrective (non-additive) interactions, but refines expert representations/weights post-selection rather than solving a joint energy over token-expert-subset assignment via gradient descent.

closest.title: DSelect-k: Differentiable Selection in the Mixture of Experts
closest.evidence: a continuously differentiable and sparse gate for MoE, based on a novel binary encoding formulation ... offers explicit control over the number of experts to select
closest.why: addresses smooth, learnable expert-subset selection but via a differentiable encoding, not an energy-based iterative refinement process capturing joint non-additive preferences.

survives: The specific mechanism of a joint energy function E(h_token, w) over continuous relaxed expert-inclusion vectors, optimized by K explicit gradient/mean-field descent steps at inference (an iterative denoising-like rewrite of the routing weights themselves, trained with a contrastive real-vs-corrupted-subset loss) is not instantiated by any of these papers, which use either static structural aggregation, message-passing among already-selected experts, or differentiable-but-single-pass gates; a genuine implementation of iterative energy descent for expert-subset selection itself would still be new.

closest.title: Toward Calibrated Mixture-of-Experts Under Distribution Shift
closest.evidence: we study how MoE models behave under distribution shift, focusing on how routing mechanisms interact with expert-level calibration
closest.why: addresses expert reliability under distribution shift at the router/expert level but via calibration/reweighting, not a persistent Kalman state fusing per-token router logits with tracked accuracy.

closest.title: Variational Routing: A Scalable Bayesian Framework for Calibrated Mixture-of-Experts Transformers
closest.evidence: VMoER confines Bayesian inference to the expert-selection stage which is typically done by a deterministic routing network
closest.why: introduces uncertainty-aware Bayesian routing at the gate but uses variational/stochastic inference, not a closed-form Kalman filter tracking per-expert reliability drift over tokens.

closest.title: Harder Tasks Need More Experts: Dynamic Routing in MoE Models
closest.evidence: our method dynamically selects experts based on the confidence level in expert selection for each input
closest.why: uses a per-token confidence signal to adjust routing but for varying k, not for down-weighting raw scores via a persistent Kalman reliability state per expert.

survives: No paper maintains a per-expert Kalman filter state (mean+variance of accuracy) updated from observed loss/correctness and fuses it via inverse-variance weighting with the raw router logit at every token; this specific online recursive Bayesian fusion mechanism for expert trustworthiness tracking is not covered by calibration, variational-routing, or confidence-based dynamic-k approaches.

closest.evidence: we introduce Expert-Space Exploration Reinforcement Learning (ESRL), an architecture-aware framework that explicitly explores the expert-routing space of MoE models... perturbation strength is further adapted according to router entropy

closest.title: Bayesian Mixture-of-Experts: Towards Making LLMs Know What They Don't Know
closest.evidence: Instead of forcing a single, deterministic expert selection, our approach models a probability distribution over the routing decision itself... in the weight-space, the logit-space, and the final selection-space
closest.why: directly replaces deterministic top-k router selection with sampling from a posterior/probability distribution over expert choice, the same mechanism at the same component.

closest.title: Variational Routing: A Scalable Bayesian Framework for Calibrated Mixture-of-Experts Transformers

closest.why: also replaces deterministic top-k routing with a Bayesian/posterior-based stochastic selection mechanism at the router.

survives: A count-based Beta/Gaussian per-expert-token-cluster posterior updated from per-token training loss as reward, with explicit sample-at-train/mean-at-inference switching framed strictly as a bandit exploration-exploitation solution replacing load-balancing losses, is a narrow variant but not clearly distinct from the Bayesian-routing and expert-space-exploration frameworks already proposed for the identical purpose at the identical component.

closest.title: Rewiring Experts on the Fly: Continuous Rerouting for Better Online Adaptation in Mixture-of-Expert models
closest.evidence: we propose a data-free, online test-time framework that continuously adapts MoE routing decisions during text generation without external supervision or data... During the prefill stage, and later in regular intervals, we optimize the routing decisions of the model using self-supervision based on the already generated sequence... We implement this through lightweight additive vectors that only update router logits in selected layers
closest.why: This is exactly test-time training of the router only, at regular intervals, using self-supervision from the generated sequence, freezing the rest of the model — the same component, mechanism, and purpose (adapting expert selection to distribution shift at inference without labels).

closest.title: R2-T2: Re-Routing in Test-Time for Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts
closest.evidence: we propose a novel and efficient method "Re-Routing in Test-Time (R2-T2)" that locally optimizes the vector of routing weights in test-time... without training any base-model parameters
closest.why: Also optimizes only router outputs at test time per-sample while freezing the base model, matching the placement and purpose even though the optimization strategy differs (neighbor search vs SGD proxy loss).

closest.title: Local Mixtures of Experts: Essentially Free Test-Time Training via Model Merging
closest.evidence: We show that TTMM is an approximation of test-time training (TTT), which fine-tunes an expert model for each prediction task, i.e., prompt.
closest.why: Explicitly frames MoE-based test-time training as approximating TTT for adapting to the input at inference, though it merges/adapts experts rather than only router parameters.

survives: The proposal's twist of updating only a small subset of router parameters via a hindsight-teacher-forced next-token loss (rather than additive router-logit vectors or output-side re-weighting) is a narrow implementation difference, not a new capability, so it would need a demonstrably different self-supervised objective or theoretical guarantee to survive as new.

closest.evidence: parameterizes the SiLU gate sharpness coefficient as a learnable function of the router logit, enabling each expert gate unit to interpolate between smooth, broadly active gating and sharp, selective gating
closest.why: adjusts gating behavior based on routing confidence but modulates gate sharpness, not a Kalman-style temporal fusion of prior logit with a downstream-error measurement.

closest.title: X-IONet: Cross-Platform Inertial Odometry Network
closest.evidence: outputs both displacement and associated uncertainty, which are further fused through an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) for robust state estimation
closest.why: uses a Kalman filter for state estimation fusion, but applied to inertial odometry displacement, not to MoE router logits.

closest.title: Spend Experts Where You Are Unsure: Confidence-Adaptive Routing for Mixture-of-Experts LoRA
closest.evidence: the router's output distribution is already a per-token uncertainty signal: peaked mass indicates confidence, while a flat distribution indicates ambiguity
closest.why: uses router confidence to adapt expert budget per token, but does not maintain temporal per-expert noise/variance state or blend prior/measurement via Kalman gain.

survives: Nothing in the set maintains a per-expert online (mean, variance) state updated causally across tokens and blends the current router logit with a downstream-error measurement via an explicit Kalman gain before top-k selection; the nearest papers either use EKF for unrelated sensor fusion or adapt routing sharpness/budget from static per-token router confidence without any temporal filtering state.

closest.title: Rewiring Experts on the Fly: Continuous Rerouting for Better Online Adaptation in Mixture-of-Expert models
closest.evidence: we propose a data-free, online test-time framework that continuously adapts MoE routing decisions during text generation without external supervision or data... using lightweight additive vectors that only update router logits in selected layers
closest.why: This adapts router logits online within a sequence based on generated context, but uses a self-supervised optimization loop rather than a causal PID error-feedback correction, and targets generic distribution shift rather than persistent per-expert load/loss drift correction via explicit P/I/D terms.

closest.title: Load Balancing Mixture of Experts with Similarity Preserving Routers
closest.evidence: We address this by introducing a novel load balancing loss that preserves token-wise relational structure, encouraging consistent expert choices for similar inputs during training.
closest.why: Addresses load balancing at the router but via an auxiliary training loss across training, not an online per-token causal feedback correction term added to logits within a sequence.

closest.title: FreeBalance: Pre-Routing Online Moe Load Balancing via Residual Workload Prediction
closest.evidence: we propose FreeBalance, a lossless online load-balancing framework that overlaps expert migration with preceding computation stages via residual workload prediction
closest.why: Online load balancing occurs but operates on expert placement/migration for inference latency, not by adding a PID-style causal correction term to the router logit itself.

survives: The proposal's distinguishing twist is a genuinely causal, per-token PID control loop (proportional+integral+derivative terms from a running error signal) added directly to each expert's router logit before top-k, correcting drift within a single sequence rather than via training-time losses, post-hoc calibration, or migration-based balancing; no paper in the set implements this specific control-theoretic online logit correction mechanism.

closest.title: FreeBalance: Pre-Routing Online Moe Load Balancing via Residual Workload Prediction
closest.evidence: FreeBalance leverages cross-layer similarities in hidden representations within the residual network to build a lightweight workload predictor... enables proactive expert migration planning before routing decisions are available
closest.why: Uses a predictive residual signal derived from cross-layer hidden-state similarity near the MoE router, but for load-balancing/prefetch scheduling, not for reshaping what the gate scores to avoid redundant expert re-selection.

closest.title: From Concentration to Differentiation and Back: Routing Effective Rank in MoE Reasoning Cohorts
closest.evidence: An exact decomposition separates cohort-wide common-mode mass from residual spectral dimensionality
closest.why: Analyzes routing via residual decomposition but as a post-hoc diagnostic of routing dynamics, not as an input transformation feeding the gate.

closest.title: Share First, Route What Remains: A Unified Framework for Token-Adaptive MoE Computation
closest.evidence: extracting reusable computation changes both what remains and how much expert capacity the remainder needs... share first, then route what remains
closest.why: Conceptually closest in spirit (routing on what remains after removing already-explained/shared computation) but operates by subtracting shared-expert value-channel content, not a causally predicted hidden state from the previous layer's chosen expert feeding the gate score.

survives: Yes: none of these papers compute a causal, per-token predictive-coding residual (predicted next hidden state from the previous layer's chosen expert, subtracted before gating) as the actual input to the router; FreeBalance predicts workload for scheduling and Share-First subtracts shared-expert content architecturally rather than gating on an expert-attributed prediction error, so a router that scores h_t - pred(prev-expert-output) specifically to suppress redundant re-selection remains unaddressed.

closest.title: Rewiring Experts on the Fly: Continuous Rerouting for Better Online Adaptation in Mixture-of-Expert models
closest.evidence: we propose a data-free, online test-time framework that continuously adapts MoE routing decisions during text generation without external supervision or data ... we optimize the routing decisions of the model using self-supervision based on the already generated sequence
closest.why: Same component (router) and same capability (mid-sequence, gradient-free adaptation of routing based on the model's own recent generation) as the proposal, though via additive router-logit vectors optimized by self-supervised loss rather than a Hebbian outer-product update.

closest.title: STAR: Rethinking MoE Routing as Structure-Aware Subspace Learning
closest.evidence: augmenting standard learnable routing with an evolving principal subspace that tracks dominant input structure via Generalized Hebbian Algorithm (GHA)
closest.why: Uses a Hebbian-style update mechanism directly on the router to adapt routing to input structure, including test-time subspace updates, but purpose is stabilizing specialization/robustness rather than reacting to per-token downstream prediction error within a sequence.

closest.title: Adaptive Hebbian Memory Routing in Vision Transformers for Few-Shot Learning
closest.evidence: Hebbian fast-weight memory can provide temporary associative information during an episode... a lightweight MLP router to control the contribution of Hebbian memory, the strength of memory updates, and the retention of previous memory
closest.why: Combines Hebbian fast-weights with routing, but the fast-weights are applied to a memory module, not to the router's own gate weights, and the router controls memory blending rather than being itself modulated by Hebbian error feedback.

survives: The specific mechanism of an outer-product Hebbian fast-weight matrix added directly onto the router's gate weight, driven explicitly by the chosen expert's downstream prediction-error signal (not self-supervised loss on generated text or GHA-based subspace tracking), applied per-token with decay/reset within a sequence, is not demonstrated by any of these; a rigorous comparison against STAR's GHA-router and Rewiring's self-supervised router-vector update would need to show this error-driven Hebbian credit-assignment step is a genuinely distinct update rule.

closest.evidence: we derive an equivalent min-max formulation and obtain a simple online algorithm via mirror descent, yielding an efficient EMA-based routing adjustment with negligible overhead

closest.title: Adaptive and Fine-grained Module-wise Expert Pruning for Efficient LoRA-MoE Fine-Tuning
closest.evidence: prior methods enforce load balancing among experts throughout training... DMEP tracks expert utilization during training and physically removes low-utility experts

closest.title: Synergistic Intra- and Cross-Layer Regularization Losses for MoE Expert Specialization
closest.evidence: Both losses are orthogonal to the standard load-balancing loss and compatible with both the shared-expert architecture in DeepSeekMoE and vanilla top-k MoE architectures
closest.why: Still uses auxiliary loss-based mechanisms rather than a gradient-free PID bias term added directly to router logits.

survives: None of the candidates implement an explicit PID (proportional-integral-derivative) feedback controller with distinct P/I/D terms added as a non-gradient bias directly to router logits in place of an aux-loss; the nearest work (φ-Balancing) uses mirror-descent/EMA-based adjustment, which is a different control law without explicit derivative/integral gain structure, so a genuine PID formulation with Kp/Ki/Kd terms tested against matched-FLOPs aux-loss baselines would still be new.

closest.title: SR-TTT Does Not Learn Retrieval: A Correction and Mechanistic Post-Mortem of Surprisal-Aware Residual Test-Time Training

closest.title: A Hippocampus for Linear Attention

survives: The specific framing of adding a small-dimension (d/4) delta-rule memory bank in parallel with the residual stream at every block, explicitly evaluated as a token-adaptive capacity control (vs. sequence-mixing) at matched FLOPs/params against a fixed-width baseline, is not quite what DDL or the delta-rule linear-attention papers test, but DDL's gated rank-1 residual overwrite with explicit capacity/width separation is functionally the same mechanism-at-component-for-purpose, so only a very narrowly scoped empirical distinction (e.g. isolating capacity-allocation effects independent of sequence-mixing benefits) would be new.

closest.title: LARA: Lightweight Adapters in the Residual Stream for Composable Adaptation and Alignment
closest.evidence: LARA reads the hidden state at a small set of layers and adds a correction of low rank back to the residual stream, leaving all base weights untouched.
closest.why: Same component (residual stream) and low-rank adapter write mechanism, but the adapter is trained offline/statically per-behavior and selected/scaled at inference, not updated online per-token via a self-supervised test-time loss.

closest.title: Modular TTT: Rethinking Test-Time Training as Composable Modules
closest.evidence: Test-time training (TTT) views sequence modeling as an online learning problem in which fast weights are updated by an internal learning rule.
closest.why: Same TTT mechanism (online gradient update to fast weights per token) but applied to a dedicated fast-weight sequence-mixing module, not as a residual-stream write-width gate via a low-rank adapter inserted in the residual path.

closest.title: TALAN: Task-Aligned Latent Adaptation Networks for Targeted Post-Training of Large Language Models
closest.evidence: a sequence-conditioned latent side path inserted into a transformer's residual stream and co-trained with a low-rank adapter... writes them back through a controlled residual update.
closest.why: Same component and a controlled/gated residual write, but the writeback is trained in standard SFT, not via an online per-token self-supervised gradient step at test time.

survives: The key novel claim is that the adapter itself receives an online, causal, per-token gradient update from a self-supervised loss at inference (adapting write-width on the fly), which none of the closest papers do—LARA and TALAN train/select statically, and Modular TTT's online updates are not placed as a residual-write-gating adapter.

closest.title: Precision Tracked Transformer via Kalman Filtering, Kriging and Process Noise
closest.evidence: the residual connection becomes a Kalman update with adaptive gain, and the FFN becomes a dynamics model propagating precision via a Jacobian--plus--process-noise rule
closest.why: This places a closed-loop feedback controller (Kalman gain) directly on the residual-stream write, adaptively scaling each block's contribution per token, the same component and same dynamic-throttling capability as the proposed PID controller.

closest.title: Scaling Adaptive Depth with Norm-Agnostic Residual Networks
closest.evidence: NAG, a norm-agnostic residual architecture that separates magnitude from directional information in the residual stream, preserving meaningful layer contributions throughout depth and preventing later updates from being systematically suppressed by residual-norm growth
closest.why: Targets the same problem (norm growth causing diminished per-layer write contribution) and the same component, though via a different (non-feedback-loop) mechanism.

closest.title: Adaptive Initial Residual Connections for GNNs with Theoretical Guarantees
closest.evidence: we investigate an adaptive residual scheme in which different nodes have varying residual strengths
closest.why: Same idea of per-token/node adaptive residual gain rather than a fixed static scalar, though not framed as PID/error-tracking control and not in transformers.

survives: A genuine PID loop with explicit proportional-integral-derivative terms tracking a target norm (not just an adaptive/Kalman gain or magnitude-direction split) that trains only 3 scalar gains per layer while leaving the rest of the model architecture untouched could still be a distinct, narrower mechanism than BFT's Kalman-update framing, but the core capability (feedback-driven, error-tracking dynamic residual-write scaling) is already claimed by the Bayesian Filtering Transformer paper.

closest.title: LAVa: Layer-wise KV Cache Eviction with Dynamic Budget Allocation

closest.title: What Layers When: Learning to Skip Compute in LLMs with Residual Gates

closest.why: Token-wise gating of residual writes exists here, but it gates whether a whole layer writes at all (skip/no-skip), not which channel-slots within the residual width are admitted/evicted per an ARC-style recency/frequency policy.

survives: Nothing found implements an ARC-style two-list (recency vs frequency) admit/evict policy operating on residual-stream channel slots per token with causal counters and a learned mixing coefficient; the closest works either statically taper width by depth, evict KV-cache entries, or gate whole-layer/whole-branch writes rather than sub-selecting which channels a token may write to under a fixed budget — that specific mechanism-object pairing (ARC cache-replacement logic applied to residual channels) is not covered.

closest.title: On the Design of Qwen3.8-Next Architecture
closest.evidence: The residual stream is widened to four branches and read through an elementwise gate, a design we call the Gated Residual (GR).
closest.why: Gated multi-branch residual widening with elementwise per-token gating is structurally adjacent to per-band gates, but branches are learned parallel channels, not a fixed wavelet/dyadic multiresolution decomposition tied to embedding/unembedding folding.

closest.title: HPMixer: Hierarchical Patching for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
closest.evidence: The residual component is processed through a Learnable Stationary Wavelet Transform (LSWT) to extract stable, shift-invariant frequency-domain representations.
closest.why: Uses wavelet decomposition on a residual signal for multi-scale modeling, but in a time-series forecasting pipeline, not as a per-token capacity-allocation mechanism in a transformer's residual stream.

survives: Nothing in the set applies an invertible wavelet/dyadic-band split to the transformer residual-stream channel dimension itself (folded into embed/unembed) with causal per-token gating that lets easy tokens skip fine bands entirely to save effective width; the nearest works either analyze post-hoc multi-stream usage (mHC) or gate whole learned branches (Qwen Gated Residual) rather than an explicit frequency-ordered channel hierarchy, so the specific mechanism-object pairing (wavelet multiresolution on residual channels, gated per-token band engagement) remains open.

closest.title: Remember to Forget: Gated Adaptive Positional Encoding
closest.evidence: GAPE decouples distance-based suppression from token importance through a query-dependent gate that contracts irrelevant context and a key-dependent gate that preserves salient distant tokens.
closest.why: This is content-aware modulation of positional encoding, but it gates attention decay/salience rather than performing a delta-rule erase-and-write overwrite of a positional memory keyed by content.

closest.title: MapFormer: Self-Supervised Learning of Cognitive Maps with Input-Dependent Positional Embeddings
closest.evidence: Cognitive maps are learned in the model by disentangling structural relationships in the inputs from their specific content, a property that can be achieved by updating position encodings with input-dependent matrices, built as exponentials of learned combinations of Lie-algebra generators.
closest.why: This makes position encoding input-dependent (content-conditioned) but via Lie-algebra matrix exponentials, not a delta-rule associative memory overwrite mechanism, and doesn't frame it as re-keying/collapsing index via erase-then-write.

closest.title: Solar Open 2 Technical Report
closest.evidence: using no positional encoding and a gated delta rule extended to negative eigenvalues
closest.why: This applies a delta-rule mechanism in a no-PE hybrid attention architecture, but the delta rule governs the linear-attention state/token mixing, not a dedicated positional-encoding memory keyed by content for re-indexing purposes.

survives: The proposal's specific twist—an explicit per-sequence associative memory M keyed by content embeddings, updated via delta-rule erase-then-write, whose output is injected specifically as a positional-adjustment vector to let the model collapse/stretch its effective index at structural boundaries—is not demonstrated by any candidate; GAPE and MapFormer make positional encoding content-aware but through gating or Lie-algebra transforms rather than an explicit delta-rule memory-overwrite keyed by content and dedicated to re-indexing.

closest.title: DAPE: Data-Adaptive Positional Encoding for Length Extrapolation
closest.evidence: we propose a Data-Adaptive Positional Encoding (DAPE) method, which dynamically and semantically adjusts based on input context and learned fixed priors.
closest.why: Also fuses a content-adaptive signal with a fixed prior positional encoding for length extrapolation, but does not use an explicit Kalman update with per-distance uncertainty schedules distinguishing nominal vs. measurement noise.

closest.title: Extending LLMs' Context Window with 100 Samples
closest.evidence: we identify the inherent need for LLMs' attention entropy... to maintain stability and introduce a novel extension to RoPE which combines adjusting RoPE's base frequency and scaling the attention logits

survives: The specific mechanism of an explicit Kalman-style fusion combining a nominal RoPE angle (with a learned, distance-dependent uncertainty schedule from validation loss) and a content-derived positional measurement (from induction-head/attention-entropy probes), fused per-token via inverse-variance weighting, is not implemented in any of these papers, which instead use histogram filters, static/learned biases, or entropy-based rescaling without explicit dual-source uncertainty fusion.

closest.title: MDLMPE: Distribution Aware Positional Encoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models
closest.evidence: applies distance-aware Gaussian weighting, and projects the resulting pattern through a cosine basis to obtain distribution-aware positional features... angular offsets that modulate the standard RoPE phases
closest.why: Uses Gaussian-weighted distributional features to modulate RoPE angles, similar mechanism placement, but for mask-availability awareness in diffusion LMs, not for calibrated long-position uncertainty with a confidence-gated attention fallback.

closest.title: Understanding the RoPE Extensions of Long-Context LLMs: An Attention Perspective

closest.why: Identifies attention uncertainty at long positions as a failure mode of RoPE but does not propose a mixture-density head or a learned confidence-based gate to fall back to position-agnostic attention.

survives: The specific combination of an MDN head producing (mean, variance, weight) over RoPE angle per position, trained with NLL auxiliary loss, whose mixture variance is read out as a scalar to gate interpolation between position-aware and mean-pooled position-agnostic attention, is not demonstrated in any candidate; nearest works use non-mixture probabilistic positions (histogram filter) or Gaussian-weighted fusion for a different purpose (mask-awareness) without a calibrated confidence-gated fallback mechanism.

closest.title: End-to-End Test-Time Training for Long Context

closest.title: ElasticTok: Adaptive Tokenization for Image and Video

closest.title: Byte Latent Transformer: Patches Scale Better Than Tokens
closest.evidence: BLT encodes bytes into dynamically sized patches, which serve as the primary units of computation. Patches are segmented based on the entropy of the next byte, allocating more compute and model capacity where increased data complexity demands it.
closest.why: Same placement (before embedding, on raw bytes) and same capability (dynamic, input-dependent merge boundaries allocating longer patches to predictable spans) but using entropy rather than a spectral/frequency-domain criterion.

closest.title: ByteFlow: Language Modeling through Adaptive Byte Compression without a Tokenizer
closest.evidence: ByteFlow Net performs compression-driven segmentation based on the coding rate of latent representations, yielding adaptive boundaries while preserving a static computation graph via Top-$K$ selection.
closest.why: Also learns per-input dynamic byte merge boundaries at the tokenizer stage via a signal-processing-flavored (coding-rate) criterion, matching the capability though not the DCT/wavelet mechanism.

closest.title: Dynamic Multi-Byte Prediction With Hierarchical Language Models
closest.evidence: we introduce a variable-length prediction window that aligns with the latent tokens, or segments, of a hierarchical LM
closest.why: Same general byte-level hierarchical segmentation idea but focused on prediction speed rather than the tokenizer boundary mechanism itself.

survives: The specific spectral/frequency-domain locality criterion (short-time DCT/wavelet smoothness score) as the boundary-decision signal, as opposed to entropy or coding-rate criteria, is not directly shown in these papers, so a proposal isolating that mechanism's effect could still be a genuine (if narrow) contribution.

closest.title: CAT: Content-Adaptive Image Tokenization

closest.title: Layer- and Timestep-Adaptive Differentiable Token Compression Ratios for Efficient Diffusion Transformers

survives: The explicit dual mutual-information IB objective (I(Z;Y) - beta*I(Z;X)) applied specifically to byte-level LM tokenizer boundary placement, with a Gumbel-softmax boundary scorer trained jointly with a from-scratch nano LM and an inference-time beta dial, is not demonstrated by any of these; the closest works use content/complexity predictors or router losses rather than a stated rate term against raw bytes for next-token prediction, so a rigorous IB formalization at the tokenizer for language modeling would still be a distinguishable contribution if it makes the rate-distortion tradeoff explicit and provably tied to I(Z;X) rather than an implicit token-count penalty.

closest.title: WAVECLIP: Wavelet Tokenization for Adaptive-Resolution CLIP

closest.title: Multilevel Wavelet Decomposition Network for Interpretable Time Series Analysis

survives: The specific claim that both resolutions are kept as simultaneous additive channels at every sequence position (not merely a coarser pooled stream or an adaptive-exit mechanism), letting downstream layers pick resolution per-span without any explicit chunk boundary or re-tokenisation, is a finer distinction not clearly demonstrated in HRT or WAVECLIP, which still produce a single resolution-selected representation per position/stage rather than co-resident multi-resolution channels.

closest.title: CATTO: Balancing Preferences and Confidence in Language Models
closest.evidence: a calibration-aware objective that aligns predicted confidence with empirical prediction correctness, which can be combined with the original preference optimization objectives... closest.title: Beyond Post-Hoc Temperature Scaling: Bilevel Optimization for LLM Calibration
closest.evidence: Preference alignment often makes large language models (LLMs) overconfident and poorly calibrated. Traditional post-hoc temperature scaling is inherently domain-dependent... This motivates us to modify model parameters during training to improve calibration.

closest.evidence: we present a calibration-based approach to measure long-term discrepancies between a generative sequence model and the true distribution, and use these discrepancies to improve the model... state-of-the-art language models... are miscalibrated: the entropy rates of their generations drift dramatically upward over time. closest.title: On the Entropy Calibration of Language Models
closest.evidence: entropy calibration, which asks whether a language model's entropy over generations matches its log loss on human text... it has become standard practice to truncate the distribution... does miscalibration improve automatically with scale, and if not, is it theoretically possible to calibrate without tradeoffs?
closest.why: Directly measures excess entropy/codelength of the output head against reference text and studies correction (truncation/rescaling), the same purpose as the proposal's diagnostic+correction pass.

closest.title: Physics-Aware, Shannon-Optimal Compression via Arithmetic Coding for Distributional Fidelity
closest.evidence: lossless compression via arithmetic coding provides an operational measure of dataset fidelity... discrepancies-arising from miscalibration, mismodeling, or bias-manifest as an irreducible excess in codelength relative to the Shannon-optimal limit... This excess codelength defines an absolute fidelity metric, quantified directly in bits.
closest.why: Uses arithmetic coding excess codelength explicitly as a calibration/fidelity diagnostic in bits, the same mechanism-purpose pairing though applied to physics datasets rather than LM output heads.

survives: A genuinely new contribution would need the specific coupling of exact, losslessly-invertible arithmetic-coding codelength (not just entropy-rate proxies) with a provable, parameter-light rescaling map guaranteed to drive codelength to the entropy bound while preserving exact logit recovery for at-will exact/calibrated decoding—none of the closest papers combine reversibility guarantees with a provable optimality bound in this exact form.

closest.title: Sample Margin-Aware Recalibration of Temperature Scaling

closest.why: Addresses the same post-hoc output-head recalibration problem for LLM-like classifiers but explicitly rejects multi-parameter/expressive logit-distribution methods (which would include mixture heads) in favor of a scalar margin-based scaling, showing the space is contested but not with the exact mixture-head mechanism.

survives: The proposal's specific twist—grafting a K-component mixture-density head post-hoc onto preference-trained LLM next-token logits to recover multimodal calibration collapsed by RLHF/DPO—has not been directly shown; ETN establishes the post-hoc frozen-base LLM logit-recalibration setup but with a Dirichlet/evidential parameterization rather than an explicit mixture-of-softmaxes, so demonstrating that mixture-density heads specifically recover multimodal token-level uncertainty lost to preference-training collapse (not just scalar confidence calibration) would still be a novel contribution.

closest.evidence: LLMs apply an implicit threshold to internal confidence when deciding to abstain... boosting or suppressing confidence signals correspondingly decreased or increased abstention rates

closest.title: Beyond Multi-Token Prediction: Pretraining LLMs with Future Summaries

survives: Only a genuinely different twist (e.g., proving the InfoNCE negatives specifically prevent representation collapse or degenerate shortcut solutions that BYOL/summary losses do not, or showing gains transfer specifically to re-ranking tasks not covered by prior work) would be new; the core mechanism-placement-purpose triple is already demonstrated by NONTP's TCL.

closest.title: Hybrid Probabilistic Zonotopes for Identifiable and Refinable Predictive Uncertainty
closest.evidence: Sharing the bounded generator across prediction steps couples future predictions algebraically, so observing one step refines the predictive distribution at every remaining step in a single forward pass.
closest.why: This is a multi-step probabilistic output head producing calibrated multi-step uncertainty in one forward pass, but it uses zonotope generators rather than mixture-density heads and is not shown applied to next-token LM heads at fixed offsets {1,2,4}.

closest.title: Constrained Decoding with Speculative Lookaheads
closest.evidence: the draft model is used to generate lookaheads which is verified by a combination of target LLM and task-specific reward functions
closest.why: Related to using future-token proposals to drive speculative decoding, but relies on a separate draft model rather than an auxiliary mixture-density head on the same backbone's output layer.

closest.title: Reaching Beyond the Mode: RL for Distributional Reasoning in Language Models
closest.evidence: We modify the RL objective to enable models to explicitly generate multiple candidate answers in a single forward pass, internalizing aspects of inference-time search into the model's generative process.
closest.why: Shares the goal of exposing multi-modal uncertainty in one forward pass, but targets multiple final answers via RL rather than a mixture-density auxiliary head predicting tokens at future offsets.

survives: Yes: no paper places a jointly-trained mixture-density (multi-component categorical) auxiliary head specifically at offsets {1,2,4} on top of the standard next-token LM head to produce calibrated multi-modal, multi-horizon token distributions in a single forward pass for speculative/early-exit use; the closest works either use single-mode multi-token prediction, non-mixture uncertainty representations (zonotopes), or separate draft models instead of auxiliary mixture heads on the same output layer.

closest.title: DiffuSpec: Unlocking Diffusion Language Models for Speculative Decoding
closest.evidence: uses a pretrained diffusion language model (DLM) to produce multi-token drafts in a single forward pass, while remaining compatible with standard AR verifiers ... a causal-consistency path search (CPS) over this lattice that extracts a left-to-right path aligned with AR verification
closest.why: This already places a masked-diffusion denoiser as a block drafter whose output is checked/aligned against the exact causal (AR) model before being accepted, i.e. the same sampler-level mechanism (parallel diffusion fill + causal verification) for the same capability (emit a block per round with exact-model-consistent guarantee).

closest.title: Auto-Regressive Masked Diffusion Models
closest.evidence: reframe the masked diffusion process as a block-wise causal model ... computes all conditional probabilities across multiple denoising steps in a single, parallel forward pass ... supports efficient, autoregressive-style decoding
closest.why: Trains a dedicated architecture that unifies block masked-diffusion denoising with causal/AR consistency to emit multiple tokens per round, overlapping with the proposal's joint training+verification goal though without explicit rollback-on-disagreement.

closest.title: Speculative Correction: Draft-then-Refine Decoding for Diffusion Language Models
closest.evidence: Mini drafts a full response, and Flash revises it as an editable initialization ... Causal ablations indicate that completed drafts provide useful initializations
closest.why: Also implements a draft-then-refine loop combining diffusion parallel drafting with a second-pass check/refinement, closely analogous to the proposal's denoise-then-verify structure, though without an explicit exact-probability threshold rollback to per-token autoregressive re-decoding.

survives: The specific combination of a trained small denoising adapter sharing the base backbone at matched FLOPs, plus a hard per-token exact-causal-probability threshold triggering rollback to strict autoregressive re-decoding (rather than soft lattice search or another model's revision), is a narrower verification mechanism not explicitly instantiated in DiffuSpec or Speculative Correction, so a paper demonstrating exact-distribution-preserving rollback under this specific adapter setup could still be new.

closest.title: TACG: Trajectory-Aware Commit Gating for Diffusion Language Model Decoding
closest.evidence: Temporal Implicit Logits Guidance (TILG), which keeps an exponential moving average of past logits as a self-reference and contrasts the current logits against this reference in natural-parameter space
closest.why: This applies an EMA over a logit trajectory during decoding to inform commit decisions, the same mechanism at the same component (sampler/decoder) though for a different capability (gating readiness/timing of commitment in diffusion LMs rather than reducing variance of a single autoregressive token choice via noised re-forward-passes).

closest.title: M-Ped: Multi-Prompt Ensemble Decoding for Large Language Models
closest.evidence: we calculate the ensemble probability by averaging the $n$ probability distributions within the batch, utilizing this aggregated probability to generate the token
closest.why: This averages multiple forward-pass logit/probability distributions (from varied prompts) to commit a single token, closely matching the proposal's core mechanism of averaging repeated re-evaluations to pick one token, though using prompt variation rather than embedding noise and simple averaging rather than EMA.

closest.title: Prediction Intervals for Model Averaging
closest.evidence: N/A - general model averaging framework
closest.why: Not directly relevant to decoding but included as background on averaging mechanisms generally, not a close match to the sampler application.

survives: The specific combination of noised repeated re-forward-passes (embedding dropout perturbations or KV variants) generating a logit trajectory, combined with true EMA (not simple averaging) with a tuned decay beta, applied specifically to standard autoregressive token-by-token sampling for variance reduction/calibration (not diffusion commit-gating, not multi-prompt ensembling) is not exactly demonstrated, but the core idea of EMA-over-logit-trajectory at the sampler is already used in TACG and simple ensembling-to-pick-one-token is in M-Ped, making the delta narrow.

closest.title: DMax: Aggressive Parallel Decoding for dLLMs
closest.evidence: DMax reformulates decoding as a progressive self-refinement from mask embeddings to token embeddings ... enabling iterative self-revising in embedding space
closest.why: Same mechanism (continuous embedding-space iterative refinement before discretizing to a token) applied at the decoding/sampling step, but for parallel diffusion decoding speed/quality rather than per-token energy-based correction against an autoregressive softmax draft.

closest.title: Multiplex Thinking: Reasoning via Token-wise Branch-and-Merge
closest.evidence: samples K candidate tokens and aggregates their embeddings into a single continuous multiplex token ... preserves the vocabulary embedding prior and the sampling dynamics of standard discrete generation
closest.why: Same component (sampler, candidate set of K tokens with continuous embedding manipulation before commit) but purpose is preserving multi-hypothesis uncertainty for RL-optimizable reasoning, not energy-based correction of locally-plausible-but-globally-incoherent tokens via a learned contrastive energy function.

closest.title: Learning Through Energy Refinement and Manifold Projection: A Cooperative EBM-AE Framework
closest.evidence: introduces an iterative EBM→AE→EBM sampling procedure in which Langevin dynamics and autoencoder projection alternately refine generated samples ... the EBM performs energy-based refinement toward low-energy regions
closest.why: Uses an explicit learned energy function with gradient-based refinement over samples before projection, the core EBM-refinement mechanism, but applied to image generation/inpainting rather than the LLM sampler's per-token candidate set conditioned on causal context.

survives: The proposal's specific twist — a contrastively-trained scalar energy head conditioned on causal hidden state that refines a small top-k candidate list via gradient descent before snapping to one committed autoregressive token, explicitly targeting correction of locally high-probability but globally incoherent token choices — is not demonstrated at this exact combination (causal LM sampler + top-k candidate energy refinement + one-token commit) in any single paper, so a tightly scoped implementation could still be novel.

closest.title: REST: Retrieval-Based Speculative Decoding
closest.evidence: Unlike previous methods that rely on a draft language model for speculative decoding, REST harnesses the power of retrieval to generate draft tokens... without necessitating additional training.
closest.why: Same capability (retrieval-based drafting for speculative decoding verification) at the same component (sampler/drafter), but using discrete n-gram trie retrieval rather than a Hopfield energy-descent convergence mechanism.

closest.title: DReSD: Dense Retrieval for Speculative Decoding
closest.evidence: we introduce Dense Retrieval for Speculative Decoding (DReSD), a novel framework that uses approximate nearest neighbour search with contextualised token embeddings to retrieve the most semantically relevant token sequences for SD.
closest.why: Same purpose (dense embedding-based draft retrieval feeding speculative verification) at the sampler, differing mainly in retrieval mechanism (ANN vs Hopfield energy descent).

closest.title: Stochastic Attention via Langevin Dynamics on the Modern Hopfield Energy
closest.evidence: we showed that this computation is one step of gradient descent on the modern Hopfield energy, and that Langevin sampling from the corresponding Boltzmann distribution yielded stochastic attention... Lowering the temperature gave exact retrieval
closest.why: Establishes the exact mechanism (multi-step Hopfield energy descent for retrieval) the proposal reuses, though not applied to speculative-decoding drafting.

survives: A genuine twist would be showing that Hopfield energy-descent convergence (multi-step, non-causal, iterative denoising toward an attractor) produces materially better/faster multi-token draft blocks than existing dense/sparse nearest-neighbor retrieval drafters (REST/DReSD), e.g. via provable capacity/robustness advantages of the attractor dynamics rather than just swapping the retrieval index.

closest.title: Erase-then-Delta Attention: Decoupling Erase and Write Addresses in Delta-Rule Linear Attention
closest.evidence: Delta-rule linear attention improves recurrent memory updates by correcting what is already stored at the current write address before writing new content... we propose Erase-then-Delta Attention (EDA), a memory update rule that decouples where to erase from where to write
closest.why: This places delta-rule overwrite of prior fast-weight associations (erasing/rewriting a stale committed entry independent of the current write) exactly as the primary memory mechanism, not merely a base-model KV-cache attention path, differing mainly in that it decouples erase/write addresses rather than grafting a separate mixed read head onto a frozen causal LM.

closest.title: Fast Weight Attention for Continual Learning
closest.evidence: the local fast-memory example revealed at step t is the prefix-aligned pair... The common same-step association remains causal, but optimizes a different internal objective
closest.why: studies delta-rule fast-weight updates as an online learning rule operating alongside causal read-after-write semantics, the same core idea of a separate associative state updated per-token beside the causal stream.

closest.title: Kalman Delta Networks: Uncertainty-aware Associative Memory
closest.evidence: Delta-rule models learn this strength from the current token embedding but do not track confidence in the memory estimate... allowing the Kalman gain to weight each residual write by accumulated evidence
closest.why: treats delta-rule overwriting of associative memory entries (same key, updated value) as the central mechanism, differing only in adding uncertainty tracking rather than a frozen-LM graft with a mixing gate.

survives: The specific framing as a frozen-base-LM graft where only a small linear read head and mixing gate are trained to blend causal KV attention with a separately-updated delta-rule associative state (explicitly preserving emitted-token causality while allowing 'semantic rollback' of meaning) is a narrower engineering variant not explicitly tested in these papers, but the core mechanism (delta-rule overwrite of key-value associative memory decoupled from the emitted sequence) is already established as the same operation on the same object.

closest.title: Block3D: Efficient Text-to-3D Generation via Block-Wise Diffusion
closest.evidence: generates the blocks autoregressively, and jointly denoises all tokens within the current block... we introduce confidence-guided intra-block correction, which revises low-confidence tokens before each block is finalized
closest.why: same mechanism (block-wise generate-then-revise-before-finalizing via a denoising/correction step) at the same component (sampler over a committed block), but applied to 3D shape tokens rather than language text and using confidence rather than an energy/discriminator score.

closest.title: COrAL: Order-Agnostic Language Modeling for Efficient Iterative Refinement
closest.evidence: sliding blockwise order-agnostic decoding, which performs multi-token forward prediction and backward reconstruction within context windows... allows the model to iteratively refine its outputs in parallel in the sliding block
closest.why: places iterative refinement of a just-generated block inside the LM sampler itself, similar placement and purpose (revise before finalizing) though via order-agnostic backward reconstruction rather than an explicit energy/Langevin descent.

closest.title: Multi-Scale Local Speculative Decoding for Image Generation
closest.evidence: we incorporate a local rejection and resampling mechanism, enabling efficient correction of draft errors by focusing on spatial neighborhoods rather than raster-scan resampling after the first rejection
closest.why: same capability (locally undo/rewrite a just-generated span flagged as low quality) at the sampler, but via speculative rejection rather than an energy-descent process, and in image rather than text domain.

survives: The specific twist of using an explicit trained energy function (Langevin/iterative denoising descent over soft embeddings or discrete neighborhoods, contrastively trained MLP head) as the revision criterion, rather than confidence scores, order-agnostic reconstruction, or speculative rejection, is not directly shown in these papers and could still be new if it demonstrably outperforms these simpler revision signals.

closest.title: Sequential Monte Carlo Steering of Large Language Models using Probabilistic Programs

closest.title: Sampling for Quality: Training-Free Reward-Guided LLM Decoding via Sequential Monte Carlo

closest.why: Matches the proposal's bootstrap (training-free) and learned-twist variants at the same sampler component with resampling of particles.

survives: Nothing genuinely new remains; the exact mechanism (particle population at the sampler, importance weights from lookahead/reward, periodic resampling, optional trained twist via self-normalized importance sampling) is already established by Lew et al. and the twisted-SMC line, matching the generator's own nearest-known guess.

closest.title: ROCODE: Integrating Backtracking Mechanism and Program Analysis in Large Language Models for Code Generation
closest.evidence: Ideally, LLMs should rollback and resolve the occurred error in time during code generation, rather than proceed on the basis of the error and wait for post-revising after generation.
closest.why: Same capability (revisiting and rewriting a previously committed span at generation time) but via error-triggered backtracking/regeneration rather than a maintained evolving population with mutation and fitness selection across generations.

closest.title: Large Language Model based Long-tail Query Rewriting in Taobao Search
closest.evidence: we employ beam search to generate multiple candidate rewrites, and feed them into Taobao offline system to obtain the partial order... align the model with the Taobao online objectives
closest.why: Uses multi-candidate generation plus scoring/selection akin to fitness-based survivor selection, but as an offline training signal rather than an in-loop generational mutate-and-select sampler.

closest.title: Improving Diffusion Language Model Decoding through Joint Search in Generation Order and Token Space
closest.evidence: We introduce Order-Token Search to explore this space through jointly searching over generation order and token values... enabling stable pruning and efficient exploration of diverse trajectories.
closest.why: Same sampler-level goal of exploring and revising multiple trajectories/spans with a scoring-based search rather than committing to one path, though mechanism is search/pruning not evolutionary population mutation with generations.

survives: A genuine evolutionary-population loop that maintains a population across explicit generations, mutates arbitrary spans of already-committed autoregressive output via resampling, and selects survivors by a fitness function—applied to standard autoregressive LLM decoding rather than code-specific backtracking, diffusion order-search, or offline reranking—is not directly instantiated by these papers, so a careful comparison and demonstration against ROCODE-style single-shot backtracking and best-of-N/beam baselines could still be a new empirical contribution.

closest.title: Targeted Remasking: Replacing Token Editing with Token-to-Mask Refinement in Discrete Diffusion Language Models
closest.evidence: we propose Token-to-Mask (T2M) remasking, a training-free, drop-in replacement for T2T editing that resets suspected erroneous tokens back to the mask state, allowing the diffusion process to re-predict them under cleaner context
closest.why: same capability (detect-then-repair a committed token later) at the same conceptual site (post-hoc correction of already-emitted tokens), but detection is via model confidence/probability signals, not an in-band trained parity/checksum token.

closest.title: CURE: Local Uncertainty Repair for Block-Parallel Speculative Decoding
closest.evidence: our method uses predictive confidence margins to dynamically locate candidate error tokens within a block-parallel draft, expands bounded repair paths only at these fragile nodes
closest.why: also does bounded local repair of likely-wrong tokens/spans triggered by an in-band signal, but the signal is uncertainty margin rather than a trained checksum/parity token and it's applied to speculative drafts, not committed autoregressive output.

closest.title: Enhancing Automated Program Repair via Faulty Token Localization and Quality-Aware Patch Refinement
closest.evidence: analyzing context-aware token-level uncertainty fluctuations to identify suspicious or low-confidence tokens within a patch. It then applies Chain-of-Thought guided rewriting to refine only these localized tokens
closest.why: same detect-low-confidence-then-locally-regenerate pattern but uses uncertainty signals and external test feedback rather than an explicit auxiliary parity/checksum head trained jointly with the LM.

survives: Yes: none of the closest works train a dedicated auxiliary parity/syndrome-prediction head (a compressed hash/low-rank checksum of a token block) jointly with the LM and use a mismatch between predicted and recomputed syndrome as the trigger signal — they all rely on confidence/uncertainty or external verifiers rather than an ECC-style in-band cryptographic-style checksum, so the specific error-correcting-code mechanism at the sampler is not yet demonstrated.

closest.why: Concerns lossless equivalence at the sampler for speculative verification, not arithmetic-coding-based bijective bit/token remapping for retroactive replay under a changed distribution.

closest.title: Block Verification Accelerates Speculative Decoding

closest.title: A Learned Pixel-by-Pixel Lossless Image Compression Method with 59K Parameters and Parallel Decoding
closest.evidence: a learned compression system that can achieve state-of-the-art lossless compression performance
closest.why: Uses arithmetic-coding-style entropy coding conditioned on a learned model, but for image compression, not for enabling counterfactual re-sampling/replay of an LM generation under a revised distribution.

survives: A genuinely new contribution would need to show Thompson-sampling-specific posterior exploration (vs. RL/policy-gradient adapters) gives measurably better exploration-exploitation tradeoffs than the contextual-bandit/POMDP decoding policy already demonstrated in 2603.09065, but the core capability (per-position/per-prompt online selection of decoding hyperparameters via bandit-style reward feedback) is already claimed there.

closest.title: DySpec: Faster Speculative Decoding with Dynamic Token Tree Structure
closest.evidence: we employ a greedy strategy to dynamically expand the token tree at run time... Under low temperature setting, DySpec can improve the throughput... Under high temperature setting...

survives: The specific twist of a lightweight offline classifier that predicts a discrete temperature/top-k regime from token-history features before logits are used, explicitly logging a 'misprediction rate' analogous to CPU branch mispredictions, is not demonstrated in AutoDeco (which jointly predicts continuous temperature/top-p via learned heads trained end-to-end with the model) nor in the speculative-decoding papers (which predict tokens, not sampling regimes); a proposal emphasizing the branch-prediction-style discrete regime classification and misprediction diagnostic as a separate, model-untouched auxiliary module could still be novel enough to survive as a follow-up rather than a duplicate, if it is framed as clearly distinct from joint decoding-head learning already published in 2510.26697.

closest.title: TALON: Confidence-Aware Speculative Decoding with Adaptive Token Trees
closest.evidence: fails to adapt to the varying difficulty of tokens and contexts... naturally shapes the draft tree into a "deep-and-narrow" form for deterministic contexts and a "shallow-and-wide" form for uncertain branches
closest.why: Uses a cheap per-token uncertainty/difficulty signal to allocate variable extra sampling-time compute (tree width/depth) per position, the same core capability as the proposal but framed within speculative decoding tree construction rather than a top-k/temperature default path.

closest.title: Efficient Adaptive Rejection Sampling for Accelerating Speculative Decoding in Large Language Models
closest.evidence: dynamically adjusts the acceptance threshold by incorporating the target model's own predictive uncertainty, measured as 1 - max(P_target)... intelligently relaxes the acceptance criterion when the model is uncertain
closest.why: Also gates sampling-time behavior per-position on a cheap uncertainty signal (max probability), a close analogue of the proposal's margin/entropy gate, though applied to acceptance thresholds rather than switching sampling distributions/algorithms.

closest.title: AdaThinkV: Adaptive Thinking for Token-Efficient Video Reasoning
closest.evidence: learns whether to reason explicitly without offline difficulty labels... balancing its accuracy gain against additional response length
closest.why: Same dual-process fast/slow gating philosophy (cheap default vs expensive deliberation invoked selectively) but at the reasoning-mode level rather than per-token sampling distribution level.

survives: The proposal is distinctive in gating specifically the token sampling distribution itself (top-k/temperature/renormalization/lookahead at the logit level) via a fixed deterministic entropy/margin function computed on ordinary autoregressive decoding, independent of any draft-verify or tree-search infrastructure; if implemented as a lightweight, model-architecture-agnostic wrapper around standard sampling (not requiring a separate draft model or speculative verification), this concrete instantiation is not directly shown by the closest papers, which embed adaptive compute allocation inside speculative-decoding tree structures or reasoning-mode selection.

closest.why: Places a shallow-depth approximation at the prefill KV-cache to cut TTFT, but keeps the truncated states permanently rather than emitting a token then verifying/rolling back against an exact pass.

closest.title: KV Prediction for Improved Time to First Token
closest.evidence: a small auxiliary model is used to process the prompt and produce an approximation of the KV cache used by a base model ... without the need to query the auxiliary model again
closest.why: Uses a cheap draft model to approximate the KV cache for fast TTFT, the same core idea of substituting an approximate prefill for the exact one, but does not verify/roll back against the exact pass afterward.

closest.title: Speculative Prefill: Turbocharging TTFT with Lightweight and Training-Free Token Importance Estimation
closest.evidence: leverages a lightweight model to speculate locally important tokens based on the context ... then sent to the main model for processing
closest.why: Same component (prefill) and same goal (TTFT reduction via cheap speculative pass) but the speculation selects tokens to keep, not an approximate hidden-state cache that is later verified/corrected token-by-token with rollback.

survives: The specific speculate-and-verify-with-rollback loop—emitting token 1 from an approximate shallow/draft KV cache and then exactly reconciling/rolling back per-layer against the full pass before continuing generation—is not what any of these do; they either permanently truncate depth (SPEED), replace the cache once without verification (KV Prediction), or prune tokens rather than depth (SpecPrefill), so a verified, correctable approximate-prefill mechanism could still be new.

closest.title: Speculative Prefill: Turbocharging TTFT with Lightweight and Training-Free Token Importance Estimation
closest.evidence: leverages a lightweight model to speculate locally important tokens based on the context. These tokens, along with the necessary positional information, are then sent to the main model for processing.
closest.why: Uses a lightweight predictor during prefill to speed up TTFT, but it prunes tokens rather than emitting output early and rolling back on divergence.

closest.title: Stream2LLM: Overlap Context Streaming and Prefill for Reduced Time-to-First-Token (TTFT)
closest.evidence: requests contend for GPU compute and memory... uses longest common prefix matching to minimize redundant computation when input changes dynamically... update-mode (iterative refinement with cache invalidation)
closest.why: Overlaps incremental context arrival with prefill and handles cache invalidation on update, closest in spirit to committing chunks and invalidating, but it is about retrieval streaming timing, not speculative early token emission with rollback on divergence of already-emitted generation.

closest.title: TreeWY: Speculative Verification for Gated DeltaNet Hybrids
closest.evidence: verify a batch of draft tokens and then roll back the rejected ones, today's systems snapshot the full recurrent state at every draft position
closest.why: Uses rollback-on-verification for speculative decoding tokens, but the rollback target is draft continuation tokens verified against the target model, not prefill chunks whose meaning was retroactively invalidated by later prompt tokens.

survives: The proposal's core novelty is treating prefill itself as an incremental, speculatively-committed transaction where token generation begins before the full prompt is seen and a learned gate can trigger rollback of already-emitted decode tokens due to a later prompt chunk changing the meaning of earlier committed KV — no candidate paper begins emitting generation before full-prompt encoding with this kind of retroactive-invalidation rollback; nearest work either prunes tokens (SpecPrefill), streams/invalidates incoming context but not decode output (Stream2LLM), or rolls back draft continuation tokens against a fixed already-encoded prefix (TreeWY), so a system that begins *generation* after a partial prefill and rolls back *emitted* text due to prefill-chunk meaning-shift remains unaddressed.

closest.title: KV Prediction for Improved Time to First Token
closest.evidence: a small auxiliary model is used to process the prompt and produce an approximation of the KV cache used by a base model... without the need to query the auxiliary model again

survives: The specific mechanism of running several differently-approximated prefill lanes in parallel and using cross-lane agreement/voting itself as the emission trigger (with exact prefill deferred as a post-hoc arbiter only on disagreement) is not described in any candidate; nearest works either guarantee exactness via splice-and-repair (Nexus) or substitute a single cheap approximator (KV Prediction) rather than consensus among multiple lanes.

closest.title: Think in Sets for Streaming Video Token Compression
closest.evidence: optimizes a dual-branch submodular coverage objective that preserves representative current-frame content... Both branches are facility-location functions, so greedy selection retains the classical (1-1/e) approximation guarantee
closest.why: This is the same submodular facility-location greedy selection with the identical (1-1/e) guarantee, applied to token/context compression rather than prompt KV-block prefill attention.

closest.title: QUOKA: Query-Oriented KV Selection For Efficient LLM Prefill
closest.evidence: By prioritizing these low cosine similarity queries, the behavior of full attention during the prefill stage can be closely approximated... then subselecting the keys most aligned with those queries
closest.why: Targets the exact same component/purpose (sub-quadratic prefill attention via block/key selection) but uses a similarity-based heuristic selection rather than a certified submodular greedy algorithm.

closest.title: The Sparse Frontier: Sparse Attention Trade-offs in Transformer LLMs
closest.evidence: fine-grained per-query importance estimation during prefilling remains impractical... forcing a task-dependent choice between global-to-token and block-to-block selection
closest.why: Surveys block-sparse prefill selection methods broadly, confirming the space is populated but without the specific submodular coverage-guarantee mechanism.

survives: The proposal's twist is porting the exact facility-location submodular greedy algorithm with its formal (1-1/e) coverage guarantee (already used for video/token compression) specifically onto prefill KV-block attention selection, which none of the prefill sparse-attention papers do (they use similarity/oracle/learned scoring without a submodular optimality certificate) — this is a narrow but plausible gap.

closest.evidence: introducing a synthetic unitary digraph convolution based on the digraph Fourier transform... effectively converts a Transformer into a Directed Graph Neural Network (DGNN) form

closest.title: Spectral-LSH: Sub-Quadratic Prompt Compression via Krylov-Projected Locality-Sensitive Hashing
closest.evidence: approximates the dominant components of an implicit attention-kernel operator using a Krylov subspace method together with random features, avoiding explicit O(N^2) attention-kernel materialization

closest.title: Attention Frequency Modulation: Training-Free Spectral Modulation of Diffusion Cross-Attention
closest.evidence: edits token-wise pre-softmax cross-attention logits in the Fourier domain: low- and high-frequency bands are reweighted
closest.why: uses Fourier-domain manipulation of attention but for diffusion cross-attention control, not for replacing prefill self-attention token-mixing with a truncated spectral operator.

survives: Yes: no candidate implements a causal, prefill-only FFT/learned-orthogonal-transform token mixer that truncates to top-r frequency coefficients as a direct O(n log n) replacement for a subset of self-attention layers while retaining local/sink attention for near-token detail, trained end-to-end at matched parameter count; the nearest works either do general spectral transformer replacement (not prefill-specific, not causal-truncated) or spectral approximation for token compression/hashing rather than direct spectral token-mixing attention replacement.

closest.title: Prompt Cache: Modular Attention Reuse for Low-Latency Inference
closest.evidence: by precomputing and storing the attention states of these frequently occurring text segments on the inference server, we can efficiently reuse them when these segments appear in user prompts
closest.why: This is exactly the proposed mechanism: a store of cached K/V for prompt segments (system prompts, templates) reused at prefill for new prompts to skip recomputation.

closest.title: Can I Buy Your KV Cache?
closest.evidence: Let a publisher precompute a document's KV cache, and let every other agent buy the right to load it and skip prefill... loading a precomputed KV and continuing matches prefilling from scratch
closest.why: Same cross-prompt KV reuse at prefill across a corpus/session of requests to amortize quadratic cost, matching the 'growing external store queried by new prompts' idea.

closest.title: Prefix Sharing Is a Sorting Problem
closest.evidence: LLM serving reuses KV cache by exact prefix match, so when a prompt is assembled from a set of reusable pieces -- retrieved passages, tool definitions, few-shot exemplars -- the order chosen for those pieces determines how much computation can be shared
closest.why: Directly addresses reuse of KV across prompts sharing structural pieces like templates and few-shot exemplars, the same target scenario as the proposal.

survives: A genuinely new angle would require approximate (non-exact-prefix) retrieval via embedding-based kNN over non-identical but structurally similar blocks with a trained adapter correcting for context mismatch, rather than exact-match prefix/document caching as in the cited systems—but this is already anticipated by adapter-based cross-cache correction work (e.g., C2KV, cross-model KV mapping) applied to the same reuse-at-prefill goal, so the novelty margin is thin.

closest.title: MiniPIC: Flexible Position-Independent Caching in <100LOC
closest.evidence: Retrieval-augmented and agentic workloads repeatedly prefill recurring predictable structured inputs (which we call "spans") such as documents and code files. ... prefix caching in engines such as vLLM cannot reuse their KV entries unless they share identical prefixes
closest.why: Same target capability (reuse cached KV for repeated/predictable prompt spans to skip prefill computation) via hash/position-based span matching, though gating is structural rather than via an entropy/arithmetic-coding signal.

closest.title: Prefilling-dLLM: Predictive Prefilling for Long-Context Inference in Diffusion Language Models
closest.evidence: partitions the prefix into N chunks, caches their KV representations once, and selects the top-K most relevant chunks with intra-chunk token sparsity for decoding
closest.why: Also splices cached KV chunks in place of recomputation to cut prefill cost, but selection is relevance/attention-based, not entropy/code-length gated, and targets dLLMs not autoregressive causal LM prefill.

closest.title: Cross-Family Speculative Prefill: Training-Free Long-Context Compression with Small Draft Models
closest.evidence: attention-based token importance estimation can enable training-free prompt compression
closest.why: Shares the goal of skipping full computation on predictable/low-importance prompt spans during prefill, but uses attention-based importance rather than an arithmetic-coding entropy signal.

survives: The specific gating mechanism—using the model's own next-token distribution fed through an actual arithmetic coder to measure per-span code length as the compressibility criterion for splicing cached KV—is not what any of these papers do (they use hashing of identical prefixes, attention-based relevance, or importance probing instead of an entropy/code-length threshold), so a paper demonstrating that this specific online entropy-coding signal yields better precision/recall for cache-splice decisions than existing heuristics would still be a new contribution.

closest.title: A Training-free Sub-quadratic Cost Transformer Model Serving Framework With Hierarchically Pruned Attention
closest.evidence: we utilize a novel tree-search-like algorithm that estimates the top-$k$ key tokens for a given query on the fly, ... based on this observation [attention locality] ... reduces the time complexity of the attention mechanism to O(T log T)
closest.why: Same purpose (sub-quadratic prefill via exploiting attention locality to predict which prior tokens/keys to attend to) and same component (prefill attention), though via tree-search estimation rather than a trained learned-index MLP predicting offset ranges.

closest.title: CRISP: Cliff-awaRe Input-adaptive Sparse Prefilling with Structural-Mass-Motivated Routing
closest.evidence: Recent dynamic methods address this by routing heads to sparse patterns in real-time, but rely on indirect routing proxies with overhead ... We present CRISP ... which identifies and addresses two structural challenges in this dynamic routing paradigm
closest.why: Same component (prefill) and same capability (input-adaptive routing to sparse attention patterns to avoid full quadratic attention), differing in the routing signal (structural proxy vs. learned-index offset predictor) and lacking an explicit train-once auxiliary predictor with verification fallback.

closest.title: Spectral-LSH: Sub-Quadratic Prompt Compression via Krylov-Projected Locality-Sensitive Hashing
closest.evidence: avoiding explicit O(N^2) attention-kernel materialization ... applies SimHash in the resulting attention eigenspace to group similar tokens
closest.why: Same sub-quadratic prefill goal via locality-based routing of tokens to reduce attention cost, though via LSH clustering/compression rather than a learned offset-predicting index with fallback verification.

survives: A trained small MLP that predicts a concrete offset-range window per token (learned-index style, analogous to Kraska et al.) plus an explicit realized-mass verification threshold triggering fallback to exact attention is a more specific mechanism than HiP's tree-search top-k estimation or CRISP's structural-proxy routing, so a paper demonstrating this exact train-once offset-predictor-with-verification-fallback design would still be new, but the core capability (sub-quadratic prefill by exploiting attention locality to skip full attention) is already occupied by HiP and CRISP.
