closest.evidence: We bridge this gap by characterizing the minimax risk of KV cache compression in terms of the intrinsic compressibility of a cache, revealing when and how accurate compression is possible... map efficiently to prefill and autoregressive decoding while achieving minimax-optimal risk
closest.why: provides a principled, information-theoretic criterion for how much to compress the KV cache rather than a fixed ratio, directly overlapping with the MDL stopping-criterion motivation.

closest.title: STAR-KV: Low-Rank KV Cache Compression via Soft Thresholding for Adaptive Rank Control
closest.evidence: a differentiable thresholding mechanism that enables optimal rank selection at both attention-head and block levels
closest.why: adaptively selects compression rank/precision per unit rather than using a hand-tuned fixed rank, same capability (principled adaptive budget) via a different mechanism (soft-threshold rank selection vs VQ+MDL).

closest.title: Don't Waste Bits! Adaptive KV-Cache Quantization for Lightweight On-Device LLMs
closest.evidence: a learned policy that assigns bit-width proportional to token importance, minimizing expected memory and latency without sacrificing competitive accuracy
closest.why: same goal of adaptively deciding compression amount per prompt/token via a learned criterion, though using importance-based bit allocation rather than two-part MDL code length.

survives: The specific two-part MDL code-length criterion (codebook bits + index bits + residual bits) used to dynamically select codebook size per prompt at prefill, as opposed to risk-bound, thresholding, or importance-based adaptive schemes, is not directly instantiated in any candidate paper.

closest.title: Block Transformer: Global-to-Local Language Modeling for Fast Inference
closest.evidence: At the lower layers, we aggregate tokens into fixed size blocks to apply attention across the entire sequence at coarse-grained detail, to capture the global context while minimizing KV cache overhead. At upper layers, we apply attention within each block to decode individual tokens
closest.why: Uses a dyadic block-pooling hierarchy at the KV/attention level to create coarse+fine representations, the core multi-scale coarsening mechanism, but is architected for inference speed within a single prompt rather than cross-prompt cache reuse via block hashing.

closest.title: Prompt Cache: Modular Attention Reuse for Low-Latency Inference
closest.evidence: by precomputing and storing the attention states of these frequently occurring text segments on the inference server, we can efficiently reuse them when these segments appear in user prompts
closest.why: Delivers the exact target capability (amortizing prefill across prompts sharing structure/templates) but reuses exact per-segment KV rather than a multi-scale RG-coarsened pyramid.

closest.title: Sparse Prefix Caching for Hybrid and Recurrent LLM Serving
closest.evidence: store exact recurrent states at a sparse set of checkpoint positions and, on a cache hit, resume from the deepest stored checkpoint and recompute the remaining suffix exactly
closest.why: Similar hierarchical/checkpointed reuse-with-recompute-of-difference structure, but operates on recurrent states, not a trained multi-scale block-pooling pyramid over KV.

survives: The specific combination of a trained hierarchical block-pooling (dyadic-tree) summarizer applied to KV pairs across multiple scales, jointly optimized to minimize KL divergence in attention outputs, and reused/hashed at the block level across prompts, is not directly instantiated by Block Transformer (which doesn't do cross-prompt cache reuse) or Prompt Cache (which doesn't do multi-scale coarse-graining or learned pooling)—so a proposal emphasizing the learned RG-style pooling MLPs trained jointly for cross-prompt coarse reuse could still be distinguishable, though it is a close combination of existing pieces.

closest.title: FreqFormer: Hierarchical Frequency-Domain Attention with Adaptive Spectral Routing for Long-Sequence Video Diffusion Transformers

closest.title: Wavelet-Aware Anomaly Detection in Multi-Channel User Logs via Deviation Modulation and Resolution-Adaptive Attention

survives: A twist that ties wavelet detail-coefficient thresholding specifically to skipping/recomputing KV-cache entries during LLM prefill (with an inverse-transform reconstruction used directly as the cached representation and exact on-demand recomputation of discarded detail) is not explicitly done by WavSpA or FreqFormer, so a version concretely instantiated as a prefill KV-cache sparsification/allocation scheme (rather than a general attention-in-wavelet-space layer or diffusion video attention router) could still be new.

closest.title: xPress: Parallel Refinement for Diffusion Drafters in Speculative Decoding
closest.evidence: xPress is a lightweight causal refiner that reconciles the whole diffusion block at once through parallel refinement, restoring and propagating causal dependencies across the draft without a token-by-token loop.
closest.why: This applies an iterative in-place refinement pass over a whole draft block to raise mutual consistency and acceptance length, the same placement and purpose as the proposal, though framed as causal reconciliation rather than energy descent.

closest.title: LiLiCorr: Lightweight Likelihood Correlation of Parallel Drafts for Speculative Decoding
closest.evidence: It keeps the top-k tokens at each position as candidates and processes them jointly ... We further co-train the drafter with LiLiCorr, so it learns to propose candidates that correlate into longer accepted sequences.
closest.why: Same goal (block-level joint coherence to raise acceptance) achieved via a learned correlation/scoring mechanism over the draft block rather than gradient/Gibbs energy descent.

closest.title: DBLAST: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding
closest.evidence: We propose a dependent block drafter based on a low-rank latent mixture over token positions, complemented by an acceptance-oriented training objective that directly targets the expected verified length.
closest.why: Also targets whole-block joint dependency modeling (versus per-position marginals) trained against verified acceptance, matching the proposal's stated new capability.

survives: A genuinely new twist would be explicit iterative energy-descent (gradient or Gibbs coordinate steps at inference time) trained via NCE against target log-probs, as opposed to the single learned refiner/correlation pass or latent-mixture reparameterization used by xPress, LiLiCorr, and DBLAST — but this is a mechanism-level distinction on the same component for the same purpose, not a new capability.

closest.title: Test-Time Speculation
closest.evidence: we propose Test-Time Speculation (TTS)... an online distillation approach that continuously adapts the speculator at test-time... Treating the draft as the student and the target as a teacher, TTS adjusts the draft over several speculation rounds
closest.why: places online self-distillation from a frozen target teacher onto the draft model, using verification signal already produced, to continuously adapt to distribution shift at inference time with no offline retraining, exactly the claimed mechanism, component and purpose.

closest.title: When Drafts Evolve: Speculative Decoding Meets Online Learning
closest.evidence: speculative decoding inherently provides verification feedback that quantifies the deviation between the draft and target models at no additional cost. This process naturally forms an iterative 'draft commits-feedback provides-draft adapts' evolving loop
closest.why: same placement (draft model updated online from target verification feedback during decoding) for the same purpose of adapting to distribution shift without offline retraining.

closest.title: Online Speculative Decoding
closest.evidence: continuously update the (multiple) draft model(s) on observed user query data. Adapting to query distribution mitigates the shifts between the training distribution of the draft model and the query distribution... based on knowledge distillation
closest.why: foundational prior art for exactly this capability: online knowledge distillation into the draft model to track distribution shift, obviating offline retraining.

survives: Restricting the online update to only a small stopping/confidence head (rather than the draft backbone) and running distillation asynchronously off a replay buffer in a background thread is a minor implementation variant, not a new capability, since TTS/OnlineSPEC/OSD already achieve on-the-fly adaptive drafting via online distillation from target feedback.

closest.title: Draft Model Knows When to Stop: Self-Verification Speculative Decoding for Long-Form Generation
closest.evidence: we propose SVIP: Self-Verification Length Policy for Long-Context Speculative Decoding, which is a training-free dynamic length policy for speculative decoding systems that adaptively determines the lengths of draft sequences by referring to the draft entropy
closest.why: already adapts drafting/stopping length in-stream from the draft's own entropy signal, matching the proposed capability.

closest.title: SpecDec++: Boosting Speculative Decoding via Adaptive Candidate Lengths
closest.evidence: We augment the draft model with a trained acceptance prediction head to predict the conditional acceptance probability of the candidate tokens. SpecDec++ will stop the current speculation when the predicted probability that at least one token gets rejected exceeds a threshold.
closest.why: places an explicit trained stopping/confidence head on the draft model to decide draft length, the same component and purpose as the proposal.

closest.title: Test-Time Speculation
closest.evidence: TTS leverages the key insight that the token verification step already invokes the target model for each draft token, providing the training signal needed to adapt the draft at no additional cost... TTS adjusts the draft over several speculation rounds
closest.why: performs in-stream test-time adaptation of the drafter using causally available accept/reject-derived signal from verification, the same mechanism-purpose pairing as the proposal.

survives: A twist restricted to updating only a small stopping-threshold adapter (not the whole draft distribution) via self-supervised accept/reject pseudo-labels rather than teacher-logit distillation might be marginally different, but SpecDec++ and SVIP already cover threshold/length adaptation from in-stream signals, and TTS already covers verification-driven online adaptation of the draft model itself, so little room remains.

closest.title: Draft Model Knows When to Stop: Self-Verification Speculative Decoding for Long-Form Generation
closest.evidence: we propose SVIP: Self-Verification Length Policy for Long-Context Speculative Decoding, which is a training-free dynamic length policy for speculative decoding systems that adaptively determines the lengths of draft sequences by referring to the draft entropy
closest.why: same component (speculative-drafting) and same capability (a length-choice policy that predicts draft reliability to set k), but via a training-free entropy heuristic rather than a curriculum-trained head.

closest.title: Verification-Aware Training for Speculative Decoding
closest.evidence: a verification head, a lightweight jointly trained binary classifier that supervises the draft model on whether each position survives sequential verification; ... verification-adaptive weighting, which ... keeps full weight up to each sample's first rejection point
closest.why: trains a small auxiliary head on accept/reject patterns to improve draft reliability prediction, closely paralleling the proposed length-prediction head, though the ordering/curriculum mechanism differs.

closest.title: From Positionwise Confidence to Prefix Scheduling: Verifier Skipping in Speculative Decoding
closest.evidence: we compare raw confidence with learned marginal and conditional survival scores under the same policy... all three confidence signals save 9.6% to 13.5% of verifier calls
closest.why: also trains/learns confidence-based scheduling signals to decide draft/verify length, same purpose at the same component but no curriculum ordering.

survives: The specific self-paced curriculum ordering of training examples by the draft model's own current loss (mastering easy spans before hard ones) to reduce deployment-time variance is not tested by any of these papers, which either use training-free entropy signals or standard i.i.d. training of the auxiliary head—so demonstrating that curriculum ordering specifically lowers variance versus i.i.d. training of the same head would be a genuine addition.

closest.title: SpecDec++: Boosting Speculative Decoding via Adaptive Candidate Lengths
closest.evidence: We augment the draft model with a trained acceptance prediction head to predict the conditional acceptance probability of the candidate tokens. SpecDec++ will stop the current speculation when the predicted probability that at least one token gets rejected exceeds a threshold.
closest.why: This is exactly the proposed mechanism: a trained head on draft states predicting accept probability, gating draft length via a running/threshold rule, feeding an unmodified verifier.

closest.title: AdaEDL: Early Draft Stopping for Speculative Decoding via an Entropy-based Lower Bound on Token Acceptance Probability
closest.evidence: allows for early stopping of the token drafting process by approximating a lower bound on the expected acceptance probability of the drafted token based on the currently observed entropy of the drafted logits
closest.why: Same placement and purpose (per-round adaptive draft length from draft logit confidence/entropy) though training-free rather than a learned head.

closest.title: AdaEAGLE: Optimizing Speculative Decoding via Explicit Modeling of Adaptive Draft Structures
closest.evidence: AdaEAGLE leverages the Lightweight Draft Length Predictor (LDLP) module to explicitly predict the optimal number of draft tokens during inference to guide the draft model.
closest.why: Also places a small trained predictor on the draft side to adaptively set draft chunk length per round, same capability and component.

survives: Nothing distinguishes the proposal from SpecDec++'s trained acceptance-prediction head with threshold-based stopping; a genuinely new twist would need a different signal source, joint drafting/verification co-adaptation, or a different object being rewritten, none of which is present here.

closest.title: LiteStage: Latency-aware Layer Skipping for Multi-stage Reasoning

closest.title: Faster Depth-Adaptive Transformers
closest.evidence: Previous works generally build a halting unit to decide whether the computation should continue or stop at each layer... may be under-optimized and inaccurate, which results in suboptimal and unstable performance
closest.why: Identifies instability of threshold-based halting units as the same problem the proposal targets, but solves it via pre-estimation rather than feedback control.

survives: None of the candidates implement a literal PID (proportional-integral-derivative) controller with running error accumulation and derivative terms driving the per-token exit threshold; the closest works use static/heuristic thresholds or iterative search rather than closed-loop control theory, so a genuine PID-based correction of oscillation/overshoot in early-exit would still be new.

closest.title: Adaptive Computation Depth via Learned Token Routing in Transformers
closest.evidence: Each gate is a lightweight two-layer multi-layer perceptron (MLP) that produces a continuous halting probability, making the mechanism end-to-end differentiable... TSA learns difficulty-proportional routing without any explicit depth pressure
closest.why: Same component (layer-schedule, per-token depth) and same capability (adaptive per-token exit), but uses a learned differentiable gate, not a Thompson-sampling bandit posterior with online conjugate updates.

closest.title: TIDE: Token-Informed Depth Execution for Per-Token Early Exit in LLM Inference
closest.evidence: attaches tiny learned routers at periodic checkpoint layers and, at inference time, selects the earliest layer whose hidden state has converged for each token
closest.why: Same per-token depth-selection goal but uses deterministic convergence-based routers, not stochastic posterior sampling with online reward updates.

closest.title: Reward Model Routing in Alignment

closest.title: Predictive Exit: Prediction of Fine-Grained Early Exits for Computation- and Energy-Efficient Inference
closest.evidence: By incorporating a low-cost prediction engine, we propose a Predictive Exit framework ... Predictive Exit can forecast where the network will exit ... which effectively reduces the network computation cost by exiting on time without running every pre-placed exiting layer.
closest.why: This places a lightweight predictor at the exit/continue decision point to forecast the exit layer ahead of time, exactly mirroring the proposal's core mechanism of predicting the continue/exit outcome to avoid stalling on the exit-head signal.

closest.title: Resource-Constrained Edge AI with Early Exit Prediction
closest.evidence: we design a low-complexity module, namely the Exit Predictor, to guide some distinctly "hard" samples to bypass the computation of the early exits.
closest.why: Again a cheap predictor sits ahead of the exit-classifier decision to short-circuit/bypass the sequential wait for the true exit signal, the same placement and purpose as the proposal's branch-predictor table.

closest.title: LayerSkip: Enabling Early Exit Inference and Self-Speculative Decoding
closest.evidence: we present a novel self-speculative decoding solution where we exit at early layers and verify and correct with remaining layers of the model.
closest.why: Provides the speculative-execute-then-verify-and-correct pattern applied to depth/exit decisions, matching the proposal's speculative commit + cheap correction on misprediction, though via self-speculative decoding rather than a counter-based table.

survives: A hardware-branch-predictor-style, non-learned, hashed-history counter table specifically overlapping the router latency with computation (rather than replacing the exit decision itself or using a full draft/verify pass) is a narrow implementation twist, but the capability (predict exit/continue ahead of time and speculatively proceed, correcting on misprediction) is already covered by Predictive Exit and Exit Predictor combined with LayerSkip's speculative-verify-correct pattern.

closest.title: AdaDecode: Accelerating LLM Decoding with Adaptive Layer Parallelism

closest.title: Depth-adaptive Inference of Looped Language Models via Continuous Depth Batching

survives: None of the candidates implement a hash-keyed trace table that memoizes an entire recorded layer-subset execution for a recognized recurring local context (n-gram/boilerplate/copy span) with periodic KL-verified validity, as opposed to per-token confidence/halting-based adaptive depth or temporal reuse between consecutive tokens; that JIT-tracing/memoization-of-repeated-context mechanism at the layer-schedule appears genuinely absent.

closest.title: AdaPonderLM: Gated Pondering Language Models with Token-Wise Adaptive Depth
closest.evidence: Our analysis shows the learned gates allocate more computation to high-NLL (hard) tokens, exhibiting adaptive computation time behavior in a fully self-supervised setting.
closest.why: Same capability (loss/difficulty-driven per-token depth allocation, easy tokens shallow/hard tokens deep) though via a learned halting gate rather than an explicit self-paced threshold curriculum.

closest.title: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically allocating compute in transformer-based language models
closest.evidence: transformers can instead learn to dynamically allocate FLOPs (or compute) to specific positions in a sequence, optimising the allocation along the sequence for different layers across the model depth
closest.why: Establishes the same component (layer-schedule) and same general goal of per-token depth allocation learned during training, though via top-k routing rather than a self-paced loss-threshold curriculum.

closest.title: Depth Adaptive Efficient Visual Autoregressive Modeling
closest.evidence: we propose a paradigm shift from pruning entire tokens to adaptively allocating per-token computational depth
closest.why: Same idea of per-token depth as a function of difficulty, but training-free and inference-time rather than a training-time self-paced curriculum that evolves with competence.

survives: The proposal's distinguishing twist is using an explicit self-paced curriculum mechanism (an adaptively-updated per-epoch loss threshold that governs the pacing function itself, evolving as a curriculum-learning schedule rather than a differentiable learned gate/router) applied only during training with cached gating vectors reused on next occurrence — none of the closest papers implement pacing-function-style curriculum scheduling of depth tied to token re-occurrence rather than a learned per-forward-pass router, so a careful comparison against AdaPonderLM/MoD emphasizing the self-paced scheduling (vs. gated/routed) mechanism could still be novel.

closest.title: N-vium: Mixture-of-Exits Transformer for Accelerated Exact Generation

survives: The specific wavelet-coefficient-hierarchy training objective (coarse readout capturing bulk signal, deeper readouts trained as residual detail conditioned on not-yet-stopping, akin to a DWT decomposition) is a structurally different loss/parameterization from standard independent or jointly-optimized early-exit heads, and if shown to yield different accuracy/compute tradeoffs than vanilla multi-exit training, that specific residual-coefficient formulation could be a genuine (if narrow) contribution.

closest.title: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically allocating compute in transformer-based language models
closest.evidence: Our method enforces a total compute budget by capping the number of tokens (k) that can participate in the self-attention and MLP computations at a given layer... determined by the network using a top-k routing mechanism
closest.why: Same component (layer-level compute routing) and same capability (per-token depth allocation), but the router is a static backprop-trained gate, not a Hebbian fast-weight matrix updated at inference without any slow-weight update.

closest.title: Adaptive Computation Depth via Learned Token Routing in Transformers
closest.evidence: a lightweight two-layer multi-layer perceptron (MLP) that produces a continuous halting probability, making the mechanism end-to-end differentiable
closest.why: Same purpose (per-token depth gating) but the gate is a trained differentiable MLP, not a training-free Hebbian outer-product accumulator that adapts within a sequence via repetition.

closest.title: Adaptive Hebbian Memory Routing in Vision Transformers for Few-Shot Learning
closest.evidence: Hebbian fast-weight memory can provide temporary associative information during an episode... uses a lightweight MLP router to control the contribution of Hebbian memory
closest.why: Uses Hebbian fast-weights for adaptive memory routing, but the Hebbian mechanism gates memory contribution, not layer-depth/block-skipping, and the router itself is a trained MLP rather than the fast-weight matrix directly gating depth.

survives: None of the retrieved papers place a Hebbian outer-product fast-weight accumulator (updated only via decay/Hebbian rule, never touched by the optimizer) directly as the gating signal controlling per-token layer-skip depth within a streaming sequence; the closest works either use backprop-trained MLP gates for depth (MoD, TSA) or Hebbian fast-weights for a different purpose (memory contribution in few-shot learning), so a Hebbian-computed depth gate exhibiting within-sequence adaptation to repeated tokens without any slow-weight update remains unaddressed.

closest.title: Adaptive Depth in Looped Transformers: Diagnosing Learned Halting Gates and Trajectory Readouts
closest.evidence: Looped Transformers increase test-time computation by repeatedly applying a shared recurrent block. Learned halting objectives in looped Transformers typically use a single exit distribution both as the inference-time stopping rule...

closest.title: Revisiting Transformer Layer Parameterization Through Causal Energy Minimization

survives: The proposal's specific twist—an explicit scalar contrastive energy head whose gradient with respect to the block's own output drives a variable-length per-instance refinement loop with an early-stopping threshold on energy delta, trained jointly with LM loss at matched FLOPs—is not clearly instantiated in any single paper, since Hyper-SET's recurrence isn't input-adaptive-halted via a learned energy head and the looped-transformer halting work uses probability gates rather than energy-gradient descent on the representation.

closest.title: Differentiable Generalised Predictive Coding
closest.evidence: Gradient-based predictive coding optimises inferred states and weights locally in for each layer by optimising precision-weighted prediction errors that propagate from stimuli towards latent states.
closest.why: This applies iterative gradient-based error-minimization inference per layer, the same core mechanism (error e, gradient update to a local state estimate) proposed in the proposal, though not specifically instantiated as a transformer layer-schedule replacement with T-step gating.

closest.title: Predictive Coding Approximates Backprop along Arbitrary Computation Graphs
closest.evidence: predictive coding converges asymptotically (and in practice rapidly) to exact backprop gradients on arbitrary computation graphs using only local learning rules... We construct predictive coding CNNs, RNNs, and the more complex LSTMs
closest.why: Shows PC's iterative local-error inference loop applied within standard deep architectures as an alternative to feedforward computation, the same placement (per-layer iterative refinement replacing single forward pass) though for training-algorithm equivalence rather than as an inference-time transformer capability with convergence gating.

closest.title: Augmented Lagrangian Predictive Coding
closest.evidence: PC-ALM introduces recurrent dynamics in each layer's activations... aligns each weight update toward BP by accumulating per-layer constraint errors into a layer-local Lagrange multiplier
closest.why: Also inserts per-layer iterative recurrent error-driven refinement of local activations, matching the mechanism of inner-loop mu updates via local error, differing mainly in the objective (matching BP gradients) and lacking the transformer-specific gated re-application/convergence-detection framing.

survives: The proposal's specific instantiation as a drop-in replacement for the transformer residual stream at nano-scale with matched-FLOPs comparison and adaptive-T convergence-gated re-application (rather than as a biologically-motivated alternative to backprop or a generic feedforward-to-PC translation) is a narrower systems/architecture claim not directly tested in the cited PC papers, so a demonstration that this gating yields a genuinely new capability (early-exit-like convergence detection at inference within a causal transformer) could still be novel.

closest.evidence: We found a simpler selection method -- Avg-K that selects blocks through their mean aggregated hidden states, achieving lower perplexity
closest.why: Explores alternative key/block selection rules for sparse FFN but uses mean-aggregation heuristics, not submodular greedy selection with an approximation-ratio certificate.

closest.title: GLASS: Global-Local Aggregation for Inference-time Sparsification of LLMs
closest.evidence: GLASS fuses global and local signals via rank aggregation, yielding robust critical-neuron selection
closest.why: Replaces top-k neuron selection with a principled rank-aggregation rule (MAP consensus), similar spirit of certifying/justifying selection but not a submodular coverage objective with a (1-1/e) guarantee.

closest.title: Prox: Training-Free FFN Activation Sparsity via Approximate Intermediate-Channel Salience in LLMs
closest.evidence: Prox hinges on the key insight: sparse execution requires only the channel mask induced by the intermediate state, which can be constructed from the magnitude ranking of its entries
closest.why: Still uses magnitude/ranking-based top-k channel selection rather than submodular maximization with provable coverage bounds.

survives: None of the retrieved papers formulate FFN key selection as submodular maximization over a coverage/facility-location surrogate with a lazy-greedy (1-1/e) approximation certificate as a per-token, per-layer replacement for top-k; that specific mechanism-object pairing (submodular greedy with provable ratio vs ad-hoc top-k/rank-aggregation heuristics) is not covered.

closest.title: Selective Sinkhorn Routing for Improved Sparse Mixture of Experts
closest.evidence: We revisit the token-to-expert assignment as an optimal transport problem. We add constraints to ensure balanced expert utilization... derives gating scores directly from the transport map
closest.why: Applies Sinkhorn-based balanced-marginal OT routing to guarantee expert load balance, the same mechanism/purpose but at the granularity of discrete MoE experts rather than dense FFN key-value memory slots.

closest.title: DOT-MoE: Differentiable Optimal Transport for MoEfication
closest.evidence: we model neuron assignment as a balanced transport problem, utilizing differentiable Sinkhorn-Knopp iterations to enforce strict expert capacity constraints
closest.why: Uses Sinkhorn OT with hard capacity/marginal constraints directly on FFN neurons (partitioning the FFN itself), closely matching the proposal's placement inside the FFN rather than at a separate MoE gate.

closest.title: Region-Graph Optimal Transport Routing for Mixture-of-Experts Whole-Slide Image Classification
closest.evidence: region-to-expert assignment formulated as entropic optimal transport (Sinkhorn) with explicit per slide capacity marginals, enforcing balanced expert utilisation without auxiliary load-balancing losses
closest.why: Same Sinkhorn balanced-marginal mechanism for hard load-balancing guarantees, applied to MoE expert routing rather than a standard dense FFN's key-value memory.

survives: The proposal's specific twist—treating the FFN's key-value memory itself (not discrete MoE experts) as the doubly-stochastic-routed object, with capacity constraints per key/neuron in an otherwise dense, non-MoE FFN—is closest to DOT-MoE's neuron-level Sinkhorn assignment, so genuine novelty would require showing the guarantee/inspection benefit holds for a standard dense-FFN key-value view distinct from any expert partitioning, which none of the papers directly frame that way.

closest.title: HoReN: Normalized Hopfield Retrieval for Large-Scale Sequential Model Editing

closest.why: Same mechanism (iterative Hopfield energy-descent retrieval over a key-value memory attached to an MLP layer) but applied to model editing/knowledge patching rather than replacing the FFN's core forward computation end-to-end from scratch.

closest.title: Hierarchical Associative Memory, Parallelized MLP-Mixer, and Symmetry Breaking

closest.title: Transformer Feed-Forward Layers Are Key-Value Memories
closest.evidence: feed-forward layers in transformer-based language models operate as key-value memories, where each key correlates with textual patterns
closest.why: Establishes the FFN-as-key-value-memory framing the proposal builds on, but uses single-step score-and-sum, not iterative Hopfield convergence.

survives: The proposal's specific twist is training the pattern set/beta end-to-end from scratch as a direct multi-step-iteration replacement for the FFN's single matmul at matched FLOPs (rather than as a post-hoc editing/interpretability wrapper as in HoReN), which is not demonstrated in these papers.

closest.title: Towards A Unified View of Sparse Feed-Forward Network in Pretraining Large Language Model
closest.evidence: Large and sparse feed-forward layers (S-FFN) such as Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) have proven effective in scaling up Transformers model size... by only activating part of the FFN parameters conditioning on input, S-FFN improves generalization performance while keeping training and inference costs (in FLOPs) fixed.
closest.why: Same goal (decouple FFN parameter/capacity count from per-token FLOPs) but via block-wise expert routing/selection, not via a matching-pursuit/ISTA sparse code over a flat atom dictionary.

closest.title: Dynamic sparsity in tree-structured feed-forward layers at scale
closest.evidence: We study sparse, tree-structured feed-forward layers as drop-in replacements for MLP blocks... enabling conditional computation via hard hierarchical routing without a separate router network... Despite activating fewer than 5% of the feed-forward block's units per token, our models match dense baselines.
closest.why: Same placement (drop-in FFN replacement, scaled from-scratch training) and same capacity/FLOP decoupling goal, but achieved via hierarchical routing tree rather than sparse-coding/dictionary matching pursuit.

closest.title: SliceMoE: Routing Embedding Slices Instead of Tokens for Fine-Grained and Balanced Transformer Scaling
closest.evidence: We introduce SliceMoE, an architecture that routes contiguous slices of a token's hidden vector... Experts operate on their assigned slices independently, and outputs are reassembled, maintaining per-token FLOP efficiency.
closest.why: Also decouples FFN expert/atom count from fixed compute via fine-grained sparse selection, but at slice-routing granularity rather than dictionary/sparse-code atoms.

survives: None of the candidates implement the FFN as a literal learned dictionary matrix with per-token codes produced by an ISTA/matching-pursuit-style sparse encoder (rather than a discrete top-k router over blocks/experts/slices); if the specific claim is that continuous sparse-coding optimization (not discrete routing) scales atom count at fixed FLOPs and yields qualitatively different scaling behavior, that mechanism-level distinction from MoE/tree/slice routing is not directly tested by any listed paper.

closest.title: Mixture of Lookup Experts

closest.title: Parametric Retrieval Augmented Generation
closest.evidence: Parametric retrieval-augmented generation (Parametric RAG), a new RAG paradigm that integrates external knowledge directly into the parameters of feed-forward networks (FFN) of an LLM through document parameterization
closest.why: Targets the FFN as the site for injecting/expanding external knowledge/memory without full retraining, similar capacity-growth motivation but via parameterization rather than kNN search over a bank.

survives: The specific mechanism of exact top-k nearest-neighbor search over a frozen/refreshed (key,value) activation bank feeding attention-like mixing into the FFN down-projection, trained/matched at FLOPs parity as in Memorizing Transformers/kNN-LM but applied inside the FFN sublayer rather than at the output layer or via cross-attention, is not directly shown in these papers.

closest.title: Decoupling Knowledge and Reasoning in Transformers: A Modular Architecture with Generalized Cross-Attention

closest.title: HoReN: Normalized Hopfield Retrieval for Large-Scale Sequential Model Editing
closest.evidence: wraps a single MLP layer with a discrete key-value memory... retrieves edits by angular similarity on the unit hypersphere
closest.why: Uses a key-value memory attached to an MLP layer for retrieval, but relies on similarity search/Hopfield dynamics rather than a trained index model predicting bucket position to skip dense scoring, and targets editing not scaling FFN capacity.

survives: None of the papers train an auxiliary predictor that maps queries directly to bucket/position indices into a sorted FFN key array to skip dense scoring at inference (the core learned-index-structure mechanism); the nearest works either use discrete-id lookup tables (MoLE) or similarity-based key-value retrieval (HoReN), so a genuine learned-index-over-sorted-keys FFN lookup trained jointly with an auxiliary bucket-prediction loss remains unaddressed.

closest.title: D2O: Dynamic Discriminative Operations for Efficient Long-Context Inference of LLMs

closest.title: Adaptive Normalization Mamba with Multi Scale Trend Decomposition and Patch MoE Encoding
closest.evidence: AdaMamba begins with an Adaptive Normalization Block that removes non stationary components through multi scale convolutional trend extraction and channel wise recalibration, enabling consistent detrending and variance stabilization.
closest.why: Closest conceptually (multi-scale decomposition feeding a normalization block for sequence data) but uses convolutional trend extraction as a preprocessing block for time-series forecasting, not a causal wavelet transform replacing per-token LayerNorm statistics inside transformer layers.

closest.title: Learning Non-linear Wavelet Transformation via Normalizing Flow
closest.evidence: With a generalized lifting scheme as coupling layers, a factor-out layer resembling the downsampling, and parameter sharing at different levels of the model, one can train the normalizing flow to filter high-frequency elements at different levels
closest.why: Uses learnable wavelet-like multiresolution decomposition with trainable filters, but for invertible generative flow/compression, not for computing normalization statistics inside a transformer's LayerNorm.

closest.title: Wavelet-Enhanced PaDiM for Industrial Anomaly Detection
closest.evidence: WE-PaDiM applies 2D DWT to feature maps from multiple backbone layers, selects specific frequency subbands (e.g., LL, LH, HL), spatially aligns them, and concatenates them channel-wise before modeling with PaDiM's multivariate Gaussian framework.
closest.why: Applies wavelet decomposition to CNN feature maps for anomaly detection, not to replace normalization statistics in a sequential/transformer model.

survives: Yes: no candidate replaces per-token LayerNorm's mean/variance computation itself with a causal, streaming, trainable-tap wavelet multiresolution decomposition over a sliding token window inside transformer layers; the nearest works either decompose CNN feature maps or time-series inputs as a separate preprocessing/detrending block rather than reworking the normalization statistic computation at each transformer layer.

closest.title: GWT: Scalable Optimizer State Compression for Large Language Model Training
closest.evidence: applies a multilevel Haar transform to matrix gradients. GWT maintains first- and second-moment states only for the compact approximation coefficients
closest.why: closest known work applies a wavelet spectral transform to optimizer moment tensors for compression, but for memory reduction rather than for capturing cross-parameter correlated curvature via a blended low-frequency reconstruction added on top of elementwise moments.

closest.title: Natural Spectral Fusion: p-Exponent Cyclic Scheduling and Early Decision-Boundary Alignment in First-Order Optimization
closest.evidence: We realize NSF via a p-exponent extension of the second-moment term, enabling both positive and negative exponents, and implement it through cyclic scheduling.
closest.why: treats the optimizer's second moment through a spectral/frequency lens but modifies the exponent/scheduling of the scalar moment rather than transforming the moment tensor into a 2D frequency basis to share low-frequency statistics across a weight matrix.

closest.title: MicroAdam: Accurate Adaptive Optimization with Low Space Overhead and Provable Convergence
closest.evidence: We achieve this by compressing the gradient information before it is fed into the optimizer state, thereby reducing its memory footprint significantly.
closest.why: another optimizer-state compression scheme, but via generic gradient compression/error-feedback, not a 2D-DCT low-frequency blend used to model cross-parameter curvature correlations.

survives: The specific mechanism of maintaining elementwise Adam second moments alongside a small set of low-frequency 2D-DCT coefficients of that same moment tensor, blended via inverse-DCT reconstruction into the denominator to capture cross-row/column curvature correlations (not simply compress or reduce memory), does not appear in any candidate paper.

closest.title: An Efficient Compression of Deep Neural Network Checkpoints Based on Prediction and Context Modeling
closest.evidence: a prediction-based compression approach, where values from the previously saved checkpoint are used for context modeling in arithmetic coding... apply pruning and quantization of the checkpoint values
closest.why: Directly applies arithmetic coding with quantization to weights and optimizer states at checkpoint time to shrink storage while enabling near-lossless recovery, exactly the proposed component/mechanism/purpose.

closest.title: On Efficient Constructions of Checkpoints
closest.evidence: LC-Checkpoint uses quantization and priority promotion to store the most crucial information for SGD to recover, and then uses a Huffman coding to leverage the non-uniform distribution of the gradient scales
closest.why: Same idea of quantizing optimizer/gradient state and entropy-coding (Huffman, an equivalent entropy coder) it per empirical distribution to shrink checkpoints for exact/near recovery.

closest.title: ExCP: Extreme LLM Checkpoint Compression via Weight-Momentum Joint Shrinking
closest.evidence: we propose a weight-momentum joint shrinking method to utilize another important information during the model optimization, i.e., momentum... we utilize non-uniform quantization to further compress the storage of checkpoints
closest.why: Targets optimizer momentum states specifically with quantization plus entropy-style compression to shrink checkpoint size, same object and purpose.

survives: Nothing distinguishes this proposal from 2506.12000/2009.13003/ExCP, which already quantize+entropy-code optimizer moment/gradient tensors per empirical distribution purely as an I/O-path checkpoint codec; a genuinely new twist would need a different guarantee (e.g. provable bit-exact bounded-loss reconstruction certificates or exploiting cross-step redundancy in a way none of these do).

closest.title: CAME: Confidence-guided Adaptive Memory Efficient Optimization
closest.evidence: we first study a confidence-guided strategy to reduce the instability of existing memory efficient optimizers... to simultaneously achieve two goals: fast convergence as in traditional adaptive methods, and low memory usage as in memory-efficient methods

closest.title: Memory-Efficient Adaptive Optimization
closest.evidence: We describe an effective and flexible adaptive optimization method with greatly reduced memory overhead. Our method retains the benefits of per-parameter adaptivity while allowing significantly larger models and batch sizes.
closest.why: Adafactor-style factored second-moment approximation is the direct ancestor of replacing per-parameter v with a compressed per-module representation for the same adaptivity purpose.

survives: The explicit information-bottleneck training objective (minimizing I(z; raw grads) while maximizing an auxiliary decoder's predictive power for next-step gradient magnitude) as a provable, tunable compression criterion is not what Gefen, CAME, or Adafactor do—they use heuristic sharing/confidence/factorization rather than an IB loss with a trained encoder/decoder, so a rigorous IB-based ablation of exactly how much state is necessary would be a genuine (if narrow) methodological twist.

closest.evidence: Preconditioning methods address this anisotropy by wrapping extra processing around this buffer... AK-Momentum updates the momentum buffer by the canonical delta rule, so each direction is forgotten at a rate set by how often it appears
closest.why: Also modifies optimizer second-moment/momentum state per-parameter based on activation frequency, but does not pool statistics across a block hierarchy or address cold-start inheritance for newly-active parameters.

closest.title: Preservation Is Not Enough for Width Growth: Regime-Sensitive Selection of Dense LM Warm Starts
closest.evidence: We study dense width growth as a candidate-selection problem over full training states, including copied weights, optimizer moments, and scheduler state.
closest.why: Addresses transferring/inheriting optimizer moments for newly added parameters during width growth, related capability but via copy/perturbation selection rather than block-averaged RG pooling.

closest.title: Accelerate Distributed Stochastic Descent for Nonconvex Optimization with Momentum
closest.evidence: At each individual learner level traditional stochastic gradient is applied. At the meta-level (global learner level), one momentum term is applied and we call it block momentum.
closest.why: Uses a block-level momentum/aggregation concept, but across distributed workers, not across parameter-block hierarchies within a layer for moment inheritance.

survives: None of the papers pool per-parameter second-moment estimates into block-averaged coarse-grained statistics that are then blended back down to initialize or correct individual parameter moments upon activation; this specific RG-style hierarchical moment-inheritance mechanism for cold-start/curvature propagation remains unaddressed.

closest.title: MT-DAO: Multi-Timescale Distributed Adaptive Optimizers with Local Updates

survives: The proposal's twist of using explicit per-parameter multiresolution (approximation+detail) coefficients with globally tuned per-level damping weights is essentially what GWT already implements (multilevel Haar transform maintaining moment states on the compact coefficients), so no clearly distinct capability remains.

closest.title: ExpTest: Loss-Curve Hypothesis Testing for Autonomous Learning-Rate Selection in Deep Neural Networks
closest.evidence: treats the training loss curve as an online signal and performs sequential statistical tests on theoretically motivated windows to detect convergent behavior and trigger learning-rate reductions
closest.why: Same capability (closed-loop LR adaptation from the loss curve's own shape within a run) at the same component (lr-schedule), but via statistical hypothesis testing rather than a delta-rule associative memory.

closest.title: AdaLRS: Loss-Guided Adaptive Learning Rate Search for Efficient Foundation Model Pretraining
closest.evidence: conducts online optimal learning rate search via optimizing loss descent velocities... Relying solely on training loss dynamics, AdaLRS involves few extra computations to guide the search process
closest.why: Same purpose (online, loss-trajectory-driven LR control replacing a fixed schedule) at the same component, differing only in the readout mechanism (velocity-based search vs delta-rule memory).

closest.title: Online Learning of a Memory for Learning Rates
closest.evidence: builds and optimizes a memory model of the optimal learning rate landscape from previously observed gradient behaviors... predicts how to scale currently observed gradients... updates its internal memory based on the observed effect
closest.why: This is a memory-based (erase/write-like) controller reading recent optimization statistics to output an LR-scaling value, the same associative-memory-as-LR-controller mechanism/purpose, differing mainly in memory formalism (not explicitly delta-rule) and gradient- vs loss-curve keys.

survives: A genuinely new angle could survive if the delta-rule's causal, in-place erase-then-write update (with formal fast-weight-programmer guarantees) is shown to give qualitatively different stability/capacity properties than the heuristic or search-based controllers in ExpTest/AdaLRS/POLA-style memories, but as stated the capability and placement are already covered.

closest.title: Robust Learning Rate Selection for Stochastic Optimization via Splitting Diagnostic

closest.title: Online Natural Gradient as a Kalman Filter

survives: No paper fuses a Kalman filter's predicted state (the prior LR schedule curve, e.g. cosine/warmup) with a noisy measurement (windowed loss-decrease/gradient-noise) via an uncertainty-weighted gain to directly set the applied per-step LR in an open-loop neural network training run; the closest work either filters model parameters (natural-gradient Kalman equivalence) or filters step-size in an unrelated adaptive-filter (AEC) context, so a Kalman-fused prior-schedule/measurement LR controller for standard NN pretraining/fine-tuning remains unaddressed.

closest.evidence: we introduce FINCH, a loss-adaptive learning-rate schedule that reduces the learning rate on high-loss batches and increases it as the model converges
closest.why: same component (LR schedule) and same mechanism family (loss-adaptive multiplicative correction) but driven by raw loss magnitude for forgetting control, not by a predictive-coding forecast-error signal for general training dynamics.

closest.title: KOALA: A Kalman Optimization Algorithm with Loss Adaptivity
closest.evidence: we propose to consider the loss as a noisy observation with respect to some reference optimum... Kalman filtering as an optimizer, as its recursive formulation is designed to estimate unknown parameters from noisy measurements
closest.why: uses an online recursive forecaster of the loss to adapt optimization, closely resembling the EMA level/slope forecaster idea, though applied to parameter updates rather than explicitly to a multiplicative LR correction gated by prediction error.

closest.title: Optimal Linear Decay Learning Rate Schedules and Further Refinements

closest.why: adapts the LR curve based on observed training statistics rather than a fixed pre-set curve, but uses gradient norms not loss-forecast error as the driving signal.

survives: The specific twist of maintaining an explicit two-scalar (level+slope) EMA forecaster of the loss and using the loss-prediction error itself (predicted vs actual loss) as a bounded multiplicative correction on a base LR curve is not exactly instantiated in KOALA (which models parameter/gradient dynamics via Kalman filtering) or FINCH (which reacts to raw loss magnitude, not forecast error); a paper isolating forecast-error-driven, hierarchical predictive-coding-style correction for general pretraining schedules would still be distinguishable.

closest.title: Better & Faster Large Language Models via Multi-token Prediction
closest.evidence: at each position in the training corpus, we ask the model to predict the following n tokens using n independent output heads, operating on top of a shared model trunk
closest.why: Same placement (per-layer/position multi-horizon heads dropped at inference) and same component (training objective), but heads are trained against raw future tokens, not against residual errors passed top-down from higher layers.

closest.title: Predictive Coding Theories of Cortical Function
closest.evidence: the bottom-up, feedforward connections in turn convey the errors between top-down predictions and actual activities. These errors are used to correct current estimates of the state of the world and generate new predictions.
closest.why: Establishes the general PC mechanism of layers learning from residual errors relative to top-down predictions, which the proposal repurposes specifically for multi-horizon token heads.

closest.title: Beyond Multi-Token Prediction: Pretraining LLMs with Future Summaries
closest.evidence: Multi-token prediction (MTP) partially mitigates these issues by predicting several future tokens at once, but it mostly captures short-range dependencies... We propose future summary prediction (FSP), which trains an auxiliary head to predict a compact representation of the long-term future
closest.why: Also modifies the training objective with auxiliary heads for multi-horizon prediction, though via summary representations rather than hierarchical residual/error factorization across depth.

survives: The specific twist of making each layer's loss the residual error unexplained by the next layer's top-down (detached) prediction at a longer horizon—an explicit hierarchical decomposition of multi-horizon prediction across depth rather than independent parallel heads or reconstruction—is not directly instantiated by any of these papers, though it is a natural combination of MTP heads (Gloeckle et al.) and classic Rao-Ballard top-down error correction.

closest.title: Learning Protein Structure-Function Relationships through Knowledge-guided Representation Decomposition

closest.title: Multi-Task Variational Information Bottleneck
closest.evidence: This article proposes an MTL model based on the architecture of the variational information bottleneck (VIB), which can provide a more effective latent representation of the input features for the downstream tasks.

survives: None of the candidates combine a per-layer VIB penalty with a fixed k-step-ahead auxiliary LM head trained jointly with next-token CE at matched FLOPs; the specific placement (future-token auxiliary head + IB bottleneck at hidden states of an autoregressive LM, ablated against a matched-FLOPs beta=0 baseline) is not addressed by any paper here, which either apply VIB to non-LM domains or to LM layers without a future-token prediction target.

closest.title: End-to-End Test-Time Training for Long Context
closest.evidence: our model continues learning at test time via next-token prediction on the given context, compressing the context it reads into its weights... a Transformer with sliding-window attention

closest.title: Training-free Context-adaptive Attention for Efficient Long Context Modeling

closest.why: targets the same capability (input-adaptive reshaping of attention connectivity mid-sequence) but via a training-free heuristic rather than gradient-based test-time training of gate parameters.

survives: A twist could survive if the gate is explicitly a per-head low-rank bias trained once and then adapted purely to trigger connectivity/window changes (not evidence localization or general context compression) with an explicit widening-on-loss-spike mechanism validated as such, since EASE-TTT targets evidence alignment and E2E-TTT updates general fast weights rather than an explicit topology-widening gate.

closest.title: SWAA: Sliding Window Attention Adaptation for Efficient and Quality Preserving Long Context Processing
closest.evidence: preserving ‘sink’ tokens and (4) lightweight fine tuning, which mitigate the training inference mismatch

survives: A genuine PID closed-loop control law (explicit error-tracking with proportional-integral-derivative gains against a measured entropy/loss error, tuned per-head via grid search rather than learned end-to-end) is a different control mechanism than the learned/gated adaptive controllers in GSA or the dynamic-span network in the speech paper, so a strict claim about closed-loop feedback control (vs. learned/heuristic adaptation) could still be a narrow but real twist.

closest.title: In-Context Compositional Learning via Sparse Coding Transformer

survives: The specific twist of using a small fixed dictionary of hand-designed structural topology atoms (local/sink/strided) combined via OMP/top-k sparse coding, rather than a fully learned dynamic mask or generic content dictionary, could still be novel if it demonstrably preserves interpretable structural priors and compute bound in a way DMA/BiFormer/sparse-coding-transformer do not.

closest.title: Parameter-free Adaptive Sparse Attention via Compression-Based Content Selection
closest.evidence: Because the compression profile is input-dependent, the resulting sparse mask adapts dynamically to content without learned parameters, auxiliary losses, or custom kernels.
closest.why: Uses a compression-based (description-length-adjacent) criterion computed online to select among sparse attention patterns per input, matching the proposal's mechanism and component but via gzip ratios rather than an explicit MDL model-bits + residual-bits computation with candidate topology families.

closest.title: Long-Context Modeling with Dynamic Hierarchical Sparse Attention for Memory-Constrained LLM Inference
closest.evidence: DHSA performs hierarchical routing by estimating importance at the chunk level and propagating it to token-level interactions, preserving causally important dependencies while enabling efficient sparsification.
closest.why: Also predicts attention sparsity/topology online per input while keeping backbone frozen, same component and adaptive-topology capability, though the selection criterion is a learned importance predictor rather than an MDL codelength comparison across a fixed topology family.

closest.title: Attention Sparsity is Input-Stable: Training-Free Sparse Attention for Video Generation via Offline Sparsity Profiling and Online QK Co-Clustering
closest.evidence: SVOO adopts a two-stage paradigm: (i) offline layer-wise sensitivity profiling to derive intrinsic per-layer pruning levels, and (ii) online block-wise sparse attention via a bidirectional co-clustering algorithm.
closest.why: Same idea of profiling then choosing sparsity/topology per input online, but the selection is via clustering/profiling not an explicit MDL codelength criterion over a discrete topology menu.

survives: The explicit MDL formulation—computing an actual two-part code (log topology-code + cross-entropy bits under each candidate mask on a held-out subsegment) and choosing the minimizer, over a small enumerable menu of named topologies (dense/windowed/sink/strided) shared-trained at matched budget—is a more principled, exactly-computed criterion than compression-ratio heuristics or learned importance scores, so a rigorous MDL-vs-heuristic comparison could still be a genuine contribution.

closest.title: KVSmooth: Mitigating Hallucination in Multi-modal Large Language Models through Key-Value Smoothing
closest.evidence: KVSmooth applies an exponential moving average (EMA) to both keys and values in the KV-Cache, while dynamically quantifying the sink degree of each token through the entropy of its attention distribution to adaptively adjust the smoothing strength
closest.why: This is exactly EMA-smoothed rewriting of stored keys/values in the cache to denoise the per-position representation over time, the same mechanism at the same component.

closest.title: What Matters for Aggressive Decoding-Time KV Eviction? Temporal Aggregation and Ranking Preservation
closest.evidence: we find that exponential-moving-average (EMA) aggregation makes approximately order-preserving scorer modifications largely indistinguishable... We introduce InertiaKV, an EMA-based decoding-time eviction method
closest.why: Also applies EMA over cache-related signals across decode steps, though targeted at eviction scoring rather than the KV content itself.

closest.title: ReST-KV: Robust KV Cache Eviction with Layer-wise Output Reconstruction and Spatial-Temporal Smoothing
closest.evidence: we design exponential moving average smoothing to handle temporal variations
closest.why: Uses EMA smoothing over cache statistics for eviction robustness, close but secondary to KVSmooth's direct KV rewrite.

survives: A learned per-head alpha trained end-to-end at matched FLOPs as a first-class architectural component (rather than a training-free inference-time smoothing heuristic) is the only remaining distinction, and it is a minor scale/training-recipe difference already anticipated by the proposal's own exclusion criteria.

closest.title: Erase-then-Delta Attention: Decoupling Erase and Write Addresses in Delta-Rule Linear Attention
closest.evidence: recurrent memory models should not only correct the current write, but also selectively suppress outdated memory at an independently chosen address
closest.why: this performs an in-place, causal, later-context-triggered rewrite of stored (KV-like recurrent) memory entries at an address other than the current write, i.e. the same 'clean up stale earlier state using later evidence without violating causal order' capability via a different (delta-rule) mechanism rather than Hopfield energy descent.

closest.title: Dialogue Without Limits: Constant-Sized KV Caches for Extended Responses in LLMs
closest.evidence: captures inter-token correlation with greater accuracy... iteratively refines the KV cache via lightweight updates guided by attention patterns of recent tokens
closest.why: MorphKV overwrites/refines existing KV cache entries in place using later context, the same object and causal-safety property, though motivated by compression rather than coherence consolidation.

closest.title: GRKV: Global Regression for Training-Free KV Cache Compression in Long-Context LLMs
closest.evidence: GRKV uses ridge-regression-based merge steps to distribute information from evicted tokens across retained tokens, while regularizing the updates to prevent over-smoothing
closest.why: also rewrites cached KV entries using later/aggregate information to denoise stale representations, though framed for compression not coherence.

survives: A genuinely new contribution would need to show that Hopfield energy-descent rewriting (multi-step, content-addressed, attractor-based) yields qualitatively different long-range coherence gains than the existing delta-rule erase-write or attention-guided iterative refinement schemes at matched budget, since the mechanism class (in-place causal-safe KV rewrite triggered by later context) is already occupied by EDA and MorphKV/GRKV for closely related purposes.

closest.title: Kalman Delta Networks: Uncertainty-aware Associative Memory
closest.evidence: we reformulate recurrent associative memory as a linear--Gaussian state-space model, for which the Kalman filter is the optimal recursive estimator... allowing the Kalman gain to weight each residual write by accumulated evidence and observation reliability
closest.why: This applies a Kalman-filter fused update, weighted by learned uncertainty, to the recurrent memory/cache state exactly as proposed, rather than an all-or-nothing overwrite.

survives: Only a narrow implementation difference (explicit per-slot KV cache in a standard transformer attention topology vs. linear-attention recurrent state) could remain novel, but the core mechanism—Kalman-gain-weighted fusion of new evidence into a cached state representing uncertainty—is already claimed.

closest.title: Retrospective Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Generation
closest.evidence: RetroAttention, a novel KV cache update technique that retrospectively revises past attention outputs using newly arrived KV entries from subsequent decoding steps... This breaks the fixed-attention-output paradigm and allows continual correction of prior approximations.
closest.why: Same mechanism/placement: periodically correcting existing cache entries in-place using later context, streaming, to fix accumulated approximation error rather than re-encoding from scratch.

closest.title: Sequential KV Cache Compression via Probabilistic Language Tries
closest.evidence: predictive delta coding, stores only the residual of each new KV vector from the model's own prediction of it
closest.why: Same core idea of storing/propagating a compact prediction-error residual against cache entries rather than full re-encoded values.

closest.title: HeadQ: Model-Visible Distortion and Score-Space Correction for KV-Cache Quantization
closest.evidence: stores a low-rank residual side code in a calibration-learned query basis and applies it as an additive logit correction... fixed-attention readout gives an A^2-weighted token-distortion surrogate
closest.why: Same operation of adding a learned residual correction to cached value/key representations to correct persistent error cheaply, applied forward at read time.

survives: Little room remains unless the predictive-coding framing yields a demonstrably different training/inference behavior (e.g. explicit top-down generative prediction rather than a learned residual/delta), but as an in-place additive correction to cached values driven by prediction error it is functionally covered by RetroAttention's retrospective revision and delta-coding/residual-correction approaches already in the pool.

closest.title: A Probabilistic Interpretation of KV Cache Eviction
closest.evidence: show that through this probabilistic interpretation, correcting for evicted entries during decoding---a previously ignored problem---becomes feasible
closest.why: Also targets selective correction of degraded KV cache entries during decoding, but via probabilistic expectation-estimation for eviction, not ECC-style parity/syndrome detection-and-repair.

closest.title: Stop the Flip-Flop: Context-Preserving Verification for Fast Revocable Diffusion Decoding
closest.evidence: COVER constructs two attention views via KV cache override... prioritises seeds using a stability aware score that balances uncertainty, downstream influence, and cache drift
closest.why: Uses a cache-drift-aware scoring signal to selectively decide which cached states to override, analogous in spirit to a corruption signal gating selective repair, but for diffusion decoding verification not ECC syndromes.

closest.title: Does Video Memory Use What It Retrieves? A Causal Audit of Memory Specificity
closest.evidence: we test this directly with read-time memory substitution, which replaces the consumed memory value while leaving the rest of the computation unchanged
closest.why: Performs selective read-time replacement of memory/cache values, related to selective repair but as an ablation/audit tool, not a trained ECC detect-and-repair mechanism.

survives: The specific mechanism of a learned parity/checksum projection with a syndrome-threshold trigger for selective, auditable cache repair (an explicit ECC-style detect-then-correct loop trained end-to-end) is not implemented by any candidate, which instead use probabilistic correction, drift-aware verification scores, or causal substitution audits rather than a parity-check code.

closest.title: Archer: Adaptive Reuse of Cached Hidden States for Efficient Rollback in Diffusion Language Models
closest.evidence: This rollback capability distinguishes them from irreversible autoregressive generation... conventional caching assumes immutable historical states and is therefore difficult to reconcile with rollback.
closest.why: Archer addresses the same underlying tension (mutable/rewritable hidden states vs. immutable causal cache) but as a caching-efficiency fix for existing DLM rollback, not as a mechanism that grafts a bounded atomic rewrite window onto an otherwise causal autoregressive decoder.

closest.title: MotionStream: Real-Time Video Generation with Interactive Motion Controls
closest.evidence: introducing carefully designed sliding-window causal attention, combined with attention sinks... enabling constant-speed generation of arbitrarily long videos
closest.why: Uses a bounded sliding window with causal attention for streaming generation, but does not perform a bidirectional rewrite-then-commit transaction over buffered uncommitted states.

closest.title: Knot Forcing: Taming Autoregressive Video Diffusion Models for Real-time Infinite Interactive Portrait Animation
closest.evidence: a temporal knot module that overlaps adjacent chunks and propagates spatio-temporal cues via image-to-video conditioning to smooth inter-chunk motion transitions
closest.why: Overlapping buffer/window revision across chunk boundaries in a causal streaming generator is structurally similar but framed as smoothing rather than atomic commit/rollback with a gate.

survives: The proposal's twist—an explicit all-or-nothing learned commit gate that atomically accepts/discards a bidirectional rewrite pass over a bounded trailing buffer in a text-token autoregressive transformer, trained from scratch at matched FLOPs—is not demonstrated by Archer (training-free KV cache reuse for already-bidirectional DLMs) or the video-streaming window/knot papers (smoothing/sink mechanisms without atomic commit gating or rollback semantics); a genuinely novel contribution would need to show this gated atomic transaction mechanism itself, not just windowed revision or cache reuse.

closest.title: Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers
closest.evidence: a "slow" neural net learns by gradient descent to program the "fast weights" of another net through sequences of elementary programming instructions which are additive outer products of self-invented activation patterns (today called keys and values)
closest.why: This establishes the exact outer-product fast-weight update A_t = decay*A_{t-1} + outer(k_t,v_t) as the core FWP mechanism the proposal reuses, but as a general sequence-modeling replacement for attention, not specifically framed as enabling 'causal-consistent revision' of a token's effective representation via later tokens.

closest.title: Fast Weight Attention for Continual Learning
closest.evidence: We study this rule under read-after-write autoregressive semantics. For the prefix-prediction objective considered here, the local fast-memory example revealed at step t is the prefix-aligned pair (x_t,y_t)=(φ(k_{t-1}),v_t)... The common same-step association (φ(k_t),v_t) remains causal, but optimizes a different internal objective.
closest.why: This paper explicitly analyzes fast-weight recurrent state under read-after-write causal semantics, i.e. the same idea that later-step updates to the fast memory affect what earlier-written positions can retrieve, which is very close to the proposal's 'update without touching stored KV' framing.

closest.title: Using Fast Weights to Attend to the Recent Past
closest.evidence: These "fast weights" can be used to store temporary memories of the recent past and they provide a neurally plausible way of implementing the type of attention to the past that has recently proved very helpful in sequence-to-sequence models.
closest.why: This is the original Hebbian fast-weight association mechanism for attending to recent tokens, matching the proposal's Hebbian outer-product update but without the explicit causal-revision framing or dual-cache-plus-fast-weight read architecture.

survives: A genuinely new contribution would need to show that the dual-path read (causal KV cache + separate short-horizon fast-weight matrix, trained jointly with matched parameter budget by trading off attention heads) produces a measurable causality-compliant 'revision' effect—i.e., that later tokens change how earlier positions are effectively read downstream—as a targeted ablation/capability claim, rather than just presenting fast-weights as an efficient attention substitute or memory augmentation as prior work does.

closest.title: Online Natural Gradient as a Kalman Filter
closest.evidence: applying an extended Kalman filter to estimate a fixed unknown parameter of a probabilistic model from a series of observations, is rigorously equivalent to estimating this parameter via an online stochastic natural gradient descent
closest.why: This equates Kalman filtering to a natural-gradient parameter update, not to fusing a noisy minibatch gradient measurement with a predicted gradient via Kalman gain at the optimizer step.

closest.title: Large-scale distributed Kalman filtering via an optimization approach
closest.evidence: we extend previous results in distributed Kalman filtering and large-scale machine learning to propose a gradient descent step for updating an estimate of the error covariance matrix
closest.why: Uses gradient descent to approximate the Kalman filter's covariance update in a distributed estimation setting, not Kalman filtering applied to fuse two gradient estimates as the optimizer's update itself.

closest.title: Rethinking Multi-Modal Learning from Gradient Uncertainty
closest.evidence: we propose Bayesian-Oriented Gradient Calibration for MML (BOGC-MML). Our approach explicitly models gradients as probability distributions to capture uncertainty... aggregating these signals using a reduced Dempster's combination rule, BOGC-MML adaptively weights gradients based on their reliability
closest.why: This fuses multiple modality-specific gradients weighted by estimated reliability, which is conceptually close but uses Dempster-Shafer fusion across modalities rather than a Kalman-gain fusion of a running gradient prediction with a fresh minibatch measurement for single-model optimization.

survives: None of the papers implement a per-step Kalman gain fusing an EMA-based gradient prediction with a fresh minibatch measurement (variance estimated from a second microbatch) to produce the applied optimizer update with a trackable fused covariance; the closest works either equate Kalman filtering to natural gradient on parameters, use gradient descent to approximate Kalman covariance updates for state estimation, or fuse cross-modal gradients via Dempster-Shafer combination — the specific placement (fusing prediction+measurement gradients via Kalman gain as the optimizer step itself) remains unaddressed.

closest.title: Evolutionary Stochastic Gradient Descent for Optimization of Deep Neural Networks
closest.evidence: ESGD combines SGD and gradient-free evolutionary algorithms as complementary algorithms in one framework in which the optimization alternates between the SGD step and evolution step to improve the average fitness of the population.
closest.why: This proposes population-based mutation/selection interleaved with SGD steps at the same component (the gradient/update step) with an explicit fitness evaluation, which is the same general mechanism (evolutionary population applied to gradient step).

closest.title: Direct From Darwin: Deriving Advanced Optimizers From Evolutionary First Principles
closest.evidence: we prove that a broad family of battle-tested optimization algorithms are already perfectly compatible with evolutionary dynamics... By simply adding DLS noise (i.e., evolutionarily faithful genetic drift), these algorithms become scientifically valid in silico simulations of Darwinian evolution.
closest.why: Also frames gradient-step optimization through evolutionary/population dynamics with structured noise, though its purpose is theoretical unification rather than fitness-based step selection.

closest.title: Stochastic Gradient Line Bayesian Optimization for Efficient Noise-Robust Optimization of Parameterized Quantum Circuits
closest.evidence: SGLBO reduces the measurement-shot cost by estimating an appropriate direction of updating circuit parameters based on stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and further utilizing Bayesian optimization (BO) to estimate the optimal step size for each iteration in SGD.
closest.why: Similar idea of evaluating candidate update directions/step sizes against a cheap validation signal before committing, though via Bayesian optimization rather than mutation/selection.

survives: The specific twist of generating explicit mutant gradient variants scaled to per-layer norm and selecting/blending via a cheap held-out microbatch fitness check (rather than alternating population evolution steps or step-size search) is a narrower, more surgical mechanism than ESGD's population-based training loop, so a tightly scoped ablation showing this exact per-step mutate-and-select filter catches bad steps that ESGD's periodic evolution phase would miss could still be novel.

closest.title: Augmented Lagrangian Predictive Coding
closest.evidence: Predictive coding (PC) is a local-learning alternative to backpropagation (BP), training deep networks via local energy-minimization dynamics rather than a global backward pass.

closest.title: Deep Predictive Coding Network for Object Recognition
closest.evidence: Feedback connections from a higher layer carry the prediction of its lower-layer representation; feedforward connections carry the prediction errors to its higher-layer... recursive cycles of bottom-up and top-down computation to update its internal representations
closest.why: Implements the identical top-down prediction / bottom-up error / iterative settling loop used to replace standard gradient computation.

survives: Only the specific gating rule (skipping/scaling a layer's update when its local error is already small) is a minor addition not explicitly tested in these papers, but it is a straightforward inference-time thresholding on the already-standard PC local error signal, not a new mechanism or placement.

closest.title: Parallel Momentum Methods Under Biased Gradient Estimations

survives: The specific closed-loop speculative-execution structure—cheap momentum/Nystrom-predicted gradient applied speculatively, verified on a small probe batch, and rolled back to exact computation on misprediction to amortize backward-pass cost below one full pass per step—is not shown in these papers; CG predict-and-recompute targets communication-hiding in a different algorithm class and lacks the probe-based verify/rollback and skip-backward capability.
